entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Offering: a gift by which a person draws near to God for the forgiveness of his sin or to give thanks.

God begins to speak to Moses, saying that when a person presents any offering, it must be of the clean animals (cattle and sheep). This offering signifies Christ, who became for us a mediator and an eternal sacrifice by which we draw near to the heavenly Father. And because the work of redemption (which belongs to Christ) has many aspects, God appointed for Moses five offerings, four of them animal sacrifices, to make clear the different aspects of this work.
The animals suitable for the burnt offering are cattle and sheep: cattle are a symbol of giving, and sheep are a symbol of sacrifice and meekness, and both are attributes of Christ.

entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Burnt offering: a sacrifice that is burned entirely on the altar.
Without blemish: having no defect, deformity or disease.
Tabernacle of the congregation: this is the church of the Old Testament.
This chapter and the chapters that follow mention five kinds of offerings: four of them are sacrifices, and the fifth is a grain offering, that is, an offering of food. These five offerings are:
1- The burnt offering (ch. 1)
2- The grain offering (ch. 2)
3- The peace offering (ch. 3)
4- The sin offering (ch. 4)
5- The trespass offering (ch. 5). These five sacrifices mentioned at the beginning of the Book of Leviticus are five aspects of the sacrifice of the Cross, as follows:
1- The burnt offering (ch. 1): in which the whole animal is burned to please God, and it signifies the sacrifice of Christ, who by His death on the Cross pleased the Father.

2- The sin offering (ch. 4, 5): part of which is burned on the altar while the rest is eaten by the priest. It signifies the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, who took away our sins and reconciled us with the Father (1 Pet 2:24). This sacrifice speaks to us of our sins directed toward others, and of course any sin against others is also against God.

3- The trespass offering (ch. 5): in which part is burned on the altar and the rest is eaten by the priest, and it speaks to us of our sins directed toward God directly. It signifies the sacrifice of Christ, who bore all kinds of sins, whether toward God or toward men.

4- The grain offering (ch. 2): in which part is presented on the altar and the rest is eaten by the priest. It signifies the life of Christ in the flesh, in which He fulfilled all righteousness for us (Mt 3:15), and in it He endured many toils throughout His life on earth.

5- The peace offering (ch. 3): in which part is burned on the altar, part is eaten by the priest, and the rest is eaten by the one who offers the sacrifice. It is the only sacrifice of which the one who offers it eats, and so it signifies the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, presented on the altar every day as Body and Blood to be eaten by those who believe in Him. The first of the five sacrifices is called the burnt offering, and it signifies Christ's obedience to the Father on behalf of humanity, and by this the Father was pleased with humanity in Christ. Therefore God is pleased with the one who offers the burnt offering, and it is the only one of the five sacrifices that no one is permitted to offer unless he is a Jew, because without faith it is impossible to please God (Heb 11:6). And since this sacrifice signifies Christ hanging on the Cross, God stipulated, as a strong indication, that it be a male without blemish.

The mention of the herd means the young bull or the full-grown ox, and it signifies spiritual manhood and steadfastness, while its being without blemish signifies that Christ was free of any sin. The slaughter takes place at the door of the tabernacle, as an indication of Christ's crucifixion outside the walls of Jerusalem.
The steps of presenting the sacrifice were five:
1- Presenting the animal before the tabernacle of the congregation, that is, before the bronze altar.
2- The one who offers it laying his hand upon it.
3- Slaughtering the animal.
4- Sprinkling its blood around the altar.
5- Burning the whole animal on the altar, as in the burnt offering, or a part of it, as in the other sacrifices.
The burnt offering was offered by a person for himself, or it was offered for the whole people (Lev 8, 9, 16, 23)... as in:
1- The burnt offering of the morning and the evening and of the Sabbath day.
2- The sacrifice of the Day of Atonement and of the other feasts.
3- The sacrifice of the beginnings of the months.
There were also burnt offerings that a person offered for himself in special cases, which are:
1- The cleansing of the leper (ch. 15)
2- The cleansing of the one with an issue.
All the preceding sacrifices were obligatory, and there were also optional or voluntary sacrifices that a person offered, which are:
1- Vows (ch. 27)

2- Freewill offerings (ch. 22:18). There are also voluntary sacrifices that the whole people could offer, as happened in the days of David when the Ark of the Covenant was brought to the city of Zion (2 Sam 6:17), and in the days of Solomon at the dedication of the Temple (1 Kgs 8:4, 5).

entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Atonement: forgiveness and covering of sin.

When the one who offers the sacrifice lays his hand on the head of the sacrifice, he declares his connection with it, indeed his union with it. The sacrifice signifies Christ, so when the one who offers it lays his hand on the sacrifice, this signifies his union with Christ, and his sins are transferred to the sacrifice, which signifies Christ. And when the sacrifice that bears the sins of the one who offers it is slaughtered, God is pleased with him. All this is a type of Christ, who bore our sins and died for us on the Cross, so that God is pleased with us when we repent and confess our sins, and in the Sacrament of Confession the priest places the cross on the head of the penitent so that his sins are transferred from his head to the head of Christ, and they are forgiven him and God is pleased with him. And when the one who offers the sacrifice lays his hand on the head of the animal, he confesses his sins, declaring that he deserves death, and by laying on his hand he is united with the animal, so that the animal is slaughtered in his place, and he thereby declares his faith in the redemption of the blood shed for him, which signifies the blood of Christ.

entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: The Levites would receive the blood in vessels when the animal was slaughtered, and then the priests would take some of this blood, which represents the life of the animal, and sprinkle it round about the bronze altar.

Christ was slaughtered on the Cross, and He was both the Priest and the sacrifice, and His blood, that is, His life which He offered, became an eternal atonement to remove the divine wrath before the throne. The blood is sprinkled in the form of a circle because the circle, which has no beginning and no end, points to the unlimited power of the blood of Christ to make atonement for sin.

entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Flay: to separate the skin from the flesh so that the inside of the sacrifice is exposed.

The one who offers the sacrifice flays the skin of the animal after slaughtering it, and then cuts its flesh into pieces at its various joints. The skin is taken by the priest (ch. 7, 8), while the pieces of flesh, which have become exposed after the skin is removed, are laid on the altar.

Here it becomes clear that Christ's obedience to the Father was not merely outward but from the depths of His being, and comprehensive of all His members, that is, His actions, and consequently it includes all the members of His Body, that is, we who believe in Him, members of His Church, so that we obey God's commandments. The cutting of the sacrifice into pieces means the exposing of every member in it, so that His obedience is complete from the heart, as we have mentioned, in addition to Christ's endurance of sufferings. And in His likeness the believer endures many toils in his spiritual striving, not only outward torments but also inward pains, because of his love for Christ.

entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Wood: dry fuel of timber that signifies the Cross; these are dry plant sticks.

The priests, the sons of Aaron, take of the holy fire that came down from heaven upon the sacrifice on the day of the anointing of Aaron and his sons, and this fire remained burning throughout the days, and with it they kindle the sacrifices. Then the priests bring some sticks of wood and kindle the fire with them so that it burns.

The fire signifies Christ's love for the Father, which reached its summit on the wood of the Cross on which He offered Himself as a sacrifice of obedience to the Father, for the fire shows the fierce sufferings that Christ endured for our sake. The Church portrays this scene when the priest holds the three candles on the cross in the prayer "God, have mercy on us" during the raising of incense, as a reference to the crucified Christ, one of the three hypostases, who brought God's mercy to the believers, removed His wrath from them, and illumined the world with His salvation.

entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Lay in order: they place the pieces of the sacrifice beside one another to give the shape of the whole animal.

The head is Christ and the pieces are we, and the fat is the best of the richness of the sacrifice, that is, the divine attributes and perfections of Christ, which make atonement for His children by His work of redemption, and the priests, by their authority, convey them to the believers through the Sacraments by the work of the fiery Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (2) The burnt offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Inwards: what is inside the sacrifice.
Legs: the two legs.
Offering made by fire: an offering to God burned with fire.

The priest washes the inside and the inwards of the animal three times, as the scholars of the Jews say, and this signifies purity of heart, and he washes the legs as a symbol of purity of conduct, and then he burns it all with fire, and God is pleased with this love offered to Him, since it is an offering of love and not an atonement for a particular sin. Therefore the burnt offering is distinguished by the phrase "a sweet savour," just as God was pleased with the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross.

The washing with water signifies Baptism, which transfers to us the work of Christ's obedience to the Father so that our depths are cleansed by it and our conduct and nature are changed, so that the righteousness of Christ covers us and the Father is pleased with us and delights in us.

If the Holy Christ offered perfect obedience to the Father, how fitting it is for me to offer my obedience and submission as a sacrifice of love to Christ in return for His love for me, so that I obey His commandments even if they are difficult, and trust that God will support me.

entries.section: (3) The burnt offering from the flock

paragraphs.text: Sheep: lambs.

Those who are not financially able may offer the burnt offering from the flock with the same ritual as before, and it is slaughtered on the right side of the altar, the side facing north (because the front of the altar faces west), because Christ's obedience to the Father brought the Father's good pleasure upon us in Christ, so that we sit at His right side, enjoying His favor. In the burnt offering of sheep everything that was said before about the burnt offering of cattle is to be observed, so it is to be a male without blemish, and after it is slaughtered its blood is sprinkled around the altar, and it is cut up and burned on the altar in the same way mentioned before for the burnt offering of cattle.

If you are not able to offer God many gifts, then offer according to your ability, even if it is something small, and trust that your gifts and your labor are very precious to God, however small, and may even be more precious in His eyes than the large gifts offered by the rich, just as He rejoiced in the widow's two mites and glorified her more than all.

entries.section: (4) The burnt offering from the birds

paragraphs.text: Turtledoves: a kind of wild dove.
Young pigeons: young doves.
Wring off: to split it around without separating it.
Crop: stomach.
Feathers: the waste of food in the belly.
Ashes: the remains of the burning.

Cleave it with the wings thereof: it was the ancient custom, when a covenant was made between two parties, that the sacrifices were split and one half placed on the right and the other half on the left, and the two parties to the covenant passed between the two halves of the split sacrifice. This signifies the covenant that the one who offers the sacrifice makes with God, by repentance and living for Him. This is the burnt offering for the one who is not financially able to offer what was mentioned before, because even the poor raise birds in their homes. The ritual of the sacrifice is as before, with the throwing of the food and its waste in the place of the ashes, because material foods are destined to perish. And the splitting of the sacrifice is a declaration of the covenant with God, but without separating it, because not a bone of Christ would be broken; He bore our sins, yet He is without sin. The turtledove is a clean bird because the Christian shrinks from sin, while the young pigeon represents meekness and humility. The flesh of the turtledove, whether young or old, is palatable, whereas of the pigeon only the young is palatable, and so God accepts the best thing, which is young pigeons. It is noted that the head of the bird is wrung off and the bird is split down the middle between the wings over the altar, because its blood is little, so the priest squeezes it out on the side of the altar.
The offering of birds as sacrifices to God was known from ancient times, for Noah offered some of them to God (Gen 8:20), and so did our father Abraham (Gen 15:9).

I hope that you will review the meekness of your character and your aversion to sin as a pure son of Christ, so that you do not mix with the wicked or sit in places that do not befit the children of God, and if you fall into sin, hasten to repentance to regain your purity.

The grain offering. The second aspect of the sacrifice of the Cross, which the grain offering makes clear, is the pure humanity of the Lord and the wonderful mystery of His Incarnation. This offering is made of wheat in the form of flour baked in different ways.

entries.section: (1) The grain offering in the form of fine flour

paragraphs.text: Fine flour: ground wheat.
Frankincense: incense.
Oil: olive oil.

Drawing near to God here is by an offering of fine flour, from which bread is made, for Christ is the source of our satisfaction because He is the bread of life, and He is the only mediator between God and men by His redeeming person and His atoning intercession. Olive oil represents the Holy Spirit, who softens the heart and lights its lamp with light and grants it peace, like the dove that came to give Noah the good news of the return of peace to the earth, with the olive branch that it carried to him. As for frankincense, it points to the prayer and worship that are offered wholly to God alone.

entries.section: (1) The grain offering in the form of fine flour

paragraphs.text: The priest takes a handful of the flour with the oil poured on it, together with all the frankincense, and lays it on the altar to be burned on it. It signifies Christ, who lived a pure life on earth to teach us how to walk in our lives, and then died on the Cross for us. The flour signifies the life of Christ in the flesh on earth, the oil the Holy Spirit who anointed Him, and the incense His worship and prayers; that is, the grain offering means Christ's purity in the flesh and His perfection in fulfilling all righteousness for us.

entries.section: (1) The grain offering in the form of fine flour

paragraphs.text: Most holy: eaten by the priests only.

The priests, that is, Aaron and his sons, eat the remainder of the grain offering in the house of the Lord, because this offering is most holy to the Lord, that is, it is eaten in His house, and likewise the showbread (Ex 35:13; ch. 24:9) and the portions of the priests from the sin offering (ch. 7:1-10; 14:13). There were some offerings that were considered holy and were eaten by the priest and his family in a clean place and not in the house of the Lord, as in the eating of the peace offerings (Num 6:20). The priest's eating of the grain offering declares:
1- God's acceptance of the offering, since His priests eat it.
2- The grace given to the priests to carry out their pastoral responsibilities and the service of God.
3- God's care for the needs of the priests and His children who are consecrated to His service and who have left the material works of the world.
Your whole life belongs to God, so take care to offer sufficient time for worship and service, like the handful of flour offered on the altar, and God will rejoice in you and bless all your works.

entries.section: (2) The grain offering in the form of baked things

paragraphs.text: Oven: a furnace.
Unleavened: dough without leaven.
Mingled: kneaded and mixed.
Wafers: thin discs of dough.
The other kind of grain offering is what is baked inside the oven, and it is of two kinds:
1- Flour kneaded with water and oil and made in the form of cakes without putting in leaven, because leaven signifies evil.
2- Flour kneaded with water and made in the form of wafers and then anointed with oil, and no leaven is put in them either, but they are unleavened.

The baked things signify Christ, who passed through sufferings for our salvation. He was conceived of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Virgin and was anointed with the Holy Spirit who descended upon Him at His baptism, and the Holy Spirit is signified by the oil with which the baked things are anointed, to declare the setting apart of His gentle, pure person, free from sin, to accomplish salvation and redemption. The unleavened bread, free of leaven, signifies the life of Christ, pure of evil, for the flour signifies the humanity of Christ and the oil the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (2) The grain offering in the form of baked things

paragraphs.text: Baking pan: a metal disc on which the baked things are placed in the oven to be done.
Part it in pieces: to break it into small parts.

The third kind of baked things is flour kneaded with water and oil and made in the form of wafers that are placed on a baking pan and put into the oven, and after they are done they are left to cool and dry, and then they are broken into small pieces and oil is poured on them. This signifies the life of Christ on earth, which was pure in all its details, for the breaking of the wafers is like the cutting of the sacrifice into pieces to show that its inside is pure.

Have you accustomed yourself to examine the details of your daily conduct before God to make sure of its purity, and to repent of your sins? For the deceiver, the devil, tries to slip in some impure little thoughts or works, so as to corrupt your heart and bring you down to greater errors. So be careful and examine yourself every day, and seek the guidance of the Holy Spirit in prayer and the counsel of your father of confession.

entries.section: (3) The grain offering in the form of dough in a frying pan

paragraphs.text: Frying pan: a deep earthen vessel.

Another kind of baked things is flour kneaded with oil and put in a frying pan and cooked in it. The pan signifies the body of the Virgin, which appears like the body of an ordinary person, and the clay signifies it, but it received great honor through the birth of Christ from it, whom the flour kneaded with oil signifies.

entries.section: (3) The grain offering in the form of dough in a frying pan

paragraphs.text: The priest takes a part of the flour kneaded with oil in the pan and lays it on the altar to be burned on it, and God is pleased with it as He was pleased with the sacrifice of His only-begotten Son, who lived a pure life on earth and offered Himself as a ransom for us on the Cross.

entries.section: (3) The grain offering in the form of dough in a frying pan

paragraphs.text: The remainder of the dough baked in the pan is eaten by the holy priests who are set apart for the service of God, and this declares God's special blessing for the priests, His servants, by which they are able to serve Him and to bind the people to the love of God.

If you serve God, know that He will give you special help and blessing to carry out His service, and in proportion to what you give in service you will receive greater help, so that you enjoy the vision of God in your life and rejoice in His work in others.

entries.section: (4) General conditions for the grain offering

paragraphs.text: God forbids the putting of leaven or honey into the grain offerings, for leaven in dough signifies the evil that works secretly in a person's heart, and honey signifies the sin that a person insists on loving, which is in his eyes as sweet as honey. This spoils a person's offerings to God, that is, God does not accept them.

entries.section: (4) General conditions for the grain offering

paragraphs.text: Oblation of the firstfruits: the offering of the firstfruits, which is the first produce of the crops or of the agricultural or animal products.

It is permissible to offer the firstfruits to the Lord even if they are of leaven or honey, because they are used as food for the servants of the altar, but it is not permissible to offer them as an offering on the altar of the Lord so that the Lord may be pleased with the one who offers it; that is, they are given to the priest and he eats of them. This is a divine declaration that leavened bread and honey are not unclean, but they signify the spiritual meanings mentioned before, so they are not offered on the altar, but a person eats them with thanksgiving from the hand of God.

entries.section: (4) General conditions for the grain offering

paragraphs.text: When you offer any offering to the Lord, you are to put salt on it, because salt preserves from corruption, so the offering with salt on it points to the humanity of Christ, which did not see corruption.

And the putting of salt on the offering signifies the covenant with God, since the ancients were accustomed, when making treaties, to eat bread and salt, in addition to the fact that salt makes food palatable.

Do not be deceived by the sweetness of sin, for it carries within it the poison of death, so keep away from everything that stirs desire, whether by sight or hearing or any other form, so that you keep yourself pure.

entries.section: (5) The offering of the firstfruits of wheat in the form of green ears

paragraphs.text: Green ears: green wheat that has not fully ripened.
Beaten out: crushed and broken.
Beaten: fine and pounded.

When the firstfruits of the wheat crop are offered to the Lord, they are to be of green ears of wheat roasted with fire, as a reference to the sufferings of Christ, who called Himself the grain of wheat, and who bore the fire of suffering and crushing in His crucifixion. The firstfruits may also be offered from wheat that is crushed and broken or from what is pounded fine. The Holy Bible mentions the offering of the firstfruits in detail in (ch. 23:9-21, 33-36), (Ex 23:14-19), (Deut 16:13-17).

entries.section: (1) The peace offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: The peace offering means obtaining peace with God. It signifies Christ, who by His redemption restored peace between us and God by taking away sin, and it is the only sacrifice of which the one who offers it is permitted to eat, that is, to partake with God in it, so it signifies Holy Communion, partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

It may be of the herd or of one of the other animals, but it must be without blemish, that is, without defect, because Christ, whom it signifies, is without sin. The herd signifies giving, since it gives milk and meat. It is noted that the burnt offering mentioned in (ch. 1) is required to be a male because it is a symbol of Christ, who pleased the Father, whereas the peace offering may be male or female, because it signifies the sharing of the believer, male or female, in partaking of the Body of Christ.

The peace offering is not to be of birds, because of the small quantity of fat in them to be offered to God on the altar (it is also mentioned in ch. 7, 17, 22, 23). The peace offering was mostly voluntary, expressing a person's thanks and love toward God, as in (ch. 7:16-21; 22:21-25), and sometimes the Law prescribed it, as in the sacrifice of consecration offered at the ordination of the priests (Ex 29:19-28; ch. 8:22-32) and the peace offering offered at the Feast of Pentecost (ch. 23:19, 20). The peace offering was preceded by a sin offering (ch. 8:14-22; 9:3, 4), and this signifies that the Sacrament of Communion is preceded by the Sacrament of Confession.

entries.section: (1) The peace offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: He shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering: to declare his thanks to God, who will allow him to eat of the blessed sacrifice offered to God, which signifies Christ.
And kill it at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: that is, before the bronze altar, because Christ gives us His salvation in the Church.

And Aaron's sons the priests shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about: the priests receive the blood in vessels and sprinkle it around the altar as a symbol of the salvation of Christ offered to the whole world from His holy altar, where we partake of His Body and Blood by means of the priests of the New Testament.

entries.section: (1) The peace offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Offering made by fire: an offering burned with fire.

Here the best part of the sacrifice, the fat, is burned as thanks to God, for thanksgiving must be from the whole heart and all the senses, outwardly and inwardly, and with the best of a person's abilities.

entries.section: (1) The peace offering from the herd

paragraphs.text: Flanks: the two sides at the waist.
The caul above the liver: the smaller lobe of the liver.

Offered to God also, along with the fat, which is the richest part of the sacrifice, are the inwards, which are the two kidneys and a part of the liver and the fat that is on them, and they signify the offering of the depths of the believer to God. All of this is burned on the altar, and God rejoices in this love.

Offer thanks to God from all your heart for His kindnesses, for no gift lacks increase except the one without thanks, and do not look upon the favors of God as ordinary things, but thanks must be offered for them.

entries.section: (2) The peace offering from the flock

paragraphs.text: Flock: goats or sheep.
Lamb: sheep, that is, those that have wool.
Peace offerings may be offered from the flock with the same ritual as the offering of cattle mentioned before in (vv. 1-5).

entries.section: (2) The peace offering from the flock

paragraphs.text: The rump: fat at the end of the tailbone, which is the fat tail, that is, the tail of the sheep.
These fats are burned with the two kidneys on the altar according to the ritual mentioned before.

God rejoices in your gifts, great or small, whatever their kind, because they express your love. So offer Him of your time and your talents and your various abilities to show your sonship to Him, and know that His fatherly love will give you more than you ask or think.

entries.section: (3) The peace offering from the goats

paragraphs.text: Here the offering is from the goats, and the same ritual is repeated as explained before and with the same meanings.

entries.section: (3) The peace offering from the goats

paragraphs.text: The fat and the blood are the richest and most precious part of the sacrifice, so they are offered to God, and it is not permitted for a person to trespass upon the portion set apart for God, in addition to the health harms of fat and its being easily spoiled and its transmitting microbes. Likewise the blood, which represents the soul of the animal and its life, which belongs to God alone, and drinking blood also transmits diseases and stirs up a person's ferocity and lusts. The Christian Church in the first Council of the Apostles (Acts 15:28, 29) decreed that Christians are not to drink blood.
Be calm and gentle in your character, for gentleness is among the fruits of the Holy Spirit, while ferocity and aggression are fruits of evil.
The sin offering

entries.section: (1) The sin offering of the priest

paragraphs.text: Commandments of the Lord concerning things which ought not to be done: things that the Lord forbids to be done.

God declares His law to the priest and the servant, and they declare it to the people. The sin offering was established for the one who sins through ignorance or weakness or forgetfulness in carrying out God's commandments, and it shows the work of Christ in forgiving our sins, whereas the one who sins deliberately, unless he repents like David (2 Sam 12:1-15), is put to death (Num 15:30). This chapter mentions some kinds of sin offerings, which are:
1- If a priest falls into sin.
2- If the people fall into sin.
3- If a ruler falls into sin.
4- If one of the individuals of the people falls into sin.

The discussion of the sin offering extends in the fifth chapter to (v. 15), where it speaks of examples of the sin offering and how those who are not able offer this sacrifice. This sacrifice was offered in the ritual of the ordination of the high priest and the priests (Ex 29:1-14), and for the purification of a woman after childbirth (ch. 12:6), and in the cleansing of those sick with diseases such as leprosy (ch. 14:19) and the bleeding and issue of men and women (ch. 15:14, 15, 29, 30), and at the feasts such as the Feast of Pentecost (ch. 23:19) and the Feast of Tabernacles (ch. 23:33-36......). It is noted that the sin offering whose blood is brought into the sanctuary is burned entirely with fire, whereas the one whose blood is not brought into the sanctuary is eaten from by the priest. The sacrifice whose blood is brought into the sanctuary is:
1- The sin offering for the priest.
2- The sin offering for the whole congregation of the people.

entries.section: (1) The sin offering of the priest

paragraphs.text: Sin according to the sin of the people: the people stumble by his sin.

If the sinner is a priest, meaning the high priest, his error is a cause of stumbling to all the people, so his sin offering is a bull. We will notice that the measure of the sin offering is determined according to the person who sins, so it is greater if he has a greater standing, such as the priest. If a person sins against his neighbor, he can make restitution to him for what he damaged for him (Ex 22:1). But here it speaks to us of sin directed toward God, which is atoned for only by the blood of Christ, whom this sacrifice signifies, so no compensation is given, but the sacrifice that signifies the unlimited sacrifice of Christ that atones for us.

entries.section: (1) The sin offering of the priest

paragraphs.text: The laying on of the hand here, on the head of the bull, is to transfer the sin from the sinner to the sacrifice when he confesses it before the Jewish priest, because Christ acted on our behalf in bearing our sins to exact their punishment in Himself, whereas the laying on of the hand in the burnt offering and the peace offering is for the union of the one who offers it with the sacrifice, to obtain its merits and its blessing.

entries.section: (1) The sin offering of the priest

paragraphs.text: Sprinkle: to sprinkle with the tip of his finger.
The veil of the sanctuary: the curtain that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies.

The priest is responsible before God for his errors, so he enters with the blood of his sacrifice before the Holy of Holies, which is the dwelling of God, to make atonement for them. And the sprinkling on the veil seven times is so that the priest may be sure that the blood of the sacrifice has atoned for his sin, so that he does not doubt the forgiveness that opens the way for his return through the veil to God, because the number seven represents perfection. The veil signifies the sin that separates man from God, which Christ removed by His death on the Cross. The number seven, which signifies the complete week, also shows that forgiveness includes the sinner throughout his life with no turning back on God's part.

It is noted that the ordinary person sprinkles the blood of his sacrifice around the bronze altar, whereas the priest sprinkles it on the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies, because the priest is responsible for the service and his sin is greater than the sin of any ordinary person since it is a cause of stumbling to others, so he asks forgiveness from before the Holy of Holies, which signifies the sanctuary and its service.

entries.section: (1) The sin offering of the priest

paragraphs.text: The altar of incense points to prayer that rises like incense before God, and its horns point to its power. Therefore the putting of the blood on the horns of the altar shows the power of the blood of the sacrifice to stand before God as a guarantee of forgiveness. And the pouring out of the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering, which signifies the Cross, points to the death of Christ and the end of His life on the Cross as an acceptable sin offering. The twofold work of the blood, within at the altar of incense and without at the altar of burnt offering, moves us to love Christ who brought us back to the Father, so that we hate the sin that shed His blood and drove us outside.

entries.section: (1) The sin offering of the priest

paragraphs.text: All the fat is gathered with the inwards, that is, the two kidneys and a part of the liver, to be burned on the altar as we mentioned in the peace offering (ch. 3:3, 4).

entries.section: (1) The sin offering of the priest

paragraphs.text: His dung: his waste.
The whole bullock: all the rest of the flesh of the bull.
Where the ashes are poured out: where the ashes are thrown outside the camp.
The camp: the place where the tents of the people are pitched and where they dwell.

The burning of the skin of the bull and its flesh and all the rest of it is outside the camp in a clean place, where it is laid on wood and burned in the place of the ashes, to show what happened to Christ when He bore our sins, for the Father hid His face from Him, and all the people rejected Him and drove Him outside their concern and asked Pilate to crucify Him, and He was crucified outside Jerusalem. For sin makes a person rejected by God and men.

It is noted that in the case of the priest's sin the whole animal is burned except the fat offered to God, whereas in the other cases of the sin offering the priest takes the skin and a part of the flesh.

Sin corrupts your life and destroys it and makes you rejected by God and men. So do not be deceived by its beauty or share in it with others, however many they may be, but let the salvation of your soul and the pleasing of God be your only goal, and you will be able to give up and trample and reject any sin.

entries.section: (2) The sin offering of the whole congregation

paragraphs.text: Sin through ignorance: they sinned unknowingly, that is, they did not know that what they did was wrong.
Hid from the eyes of the assembly: the congregation of Israel did not know that what they were doing was wrong.

The sin is known: they discovered by the grace of God that what they had done was wrong against God. The error here is the error of all the people, and those responsible for it are the leaders of the people, so they act on behalf of the people in confessing the sin by laying their hands on the head of the sacrifice.

entries.section: (2) The sin offering of the whole congregation

paragraphs.text: It is noted that the atonement for the sin of the high priest is the same as the atonement for the sin of the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that is, by offering a bull. This confirms the gravity of the priest's sin and the necessity of scrutinizing his conduct so that he does not cause others to stumble. The ritual of offering this sacrifice is the same as the ritual of offering the sacrifice for the sin of the priest, as mentioned in (vv. 3-12).

If you are a father or a mother or a servant or responsible anywhere, you are required before God for those for whom you are responsible, to teach them how to live with God and to guide them to keep away from sin. If they accept your word, you have gained their souls, and if they do not accept, their sin is on their own heads. But do not despair of their salvation throughout your life, and offer them your love and guidance and ask God to draw them to repentance and life with Him. And do not be troubled if all those around you insist on sin, but hold fast to the truth and pray for them and guide them gently and firmly as God guides you, in order to draw their hearts to repentance, even if after a while.

entries.section: (3) The sin offering of a ruler

paragraphs.text: Kid: a male goat.

The sinner here is a civil ruler among the leaders of the people, so the value of the sacrifice is lowered and it becomes a male kid of the goats, and the sinner performs the same ritual explained before.

entries.section: (3) The sin offering of a ruler

paragraphs.text: The sin offering for the ruler differs from the sin offering for the priest (vv. 3-12) in two matters:

1- The priest smears the blood on the horns of the bronze altar, which signify the power of the salvation given by God to His children, and this altar is in the outer court, whereas in the case of the priest's sin he anoints the horns of the altar of incense that is inside the Holy Place, because his sin is greater, for he is the servant of God who enters the Holy Place.

2- The sin offering of the priest, after the burning of the fat, has its flesh and everything in it burned outside the camp, whereas in the case of the ruler's sin the priest eats its flesh, and this assures the one who offers it that God has forgiven his sin, as proved by the eating of it by God's priest.

If you, beloved reader, are a servant, feel your responsibility for the sin of your people and share with them in bearing it, by caring for them and guiding them and sympathizing with them and praying for them.

entries.section: (4) The sin offering of individuals of the people

paragraphs.text: If the sinner is an individual of the people, his sacrifice is a female goat, because its price is less than the male, since his sin is less than the sin of the ruler or the priest, and the same ritual and meanings as the sacrifice of the ruler are repeated.

entries.section: (4) The sin offering of individuals of the people

paragraphs.text: Lambs (sheep) were cheaper than goats at that time, so if he is not able to buy a female goat he buys a ewe, that is, a female sheep. The ritual of this sacrifice is the same as the ritual of offering the female goat or the sin offering of the ruler.

Let each of us know his sins and grieve over them and repent, and God will forgive them to him and be pleased with him, and he will partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord, which gives salvation for us and forgiveness of sins and eternal life to the one who partakes of it. The sin offering and the trespass offering

entries.section: (1) Examples of sins and the necessity of confession

paragraphs.text: The inspired text gives three examples of sins that a person commits through ignorance, so that the one who commits them needs to offer a sin offering when he learns of them and repents. The first is if a person hears the voice of swearing and is a witness, whether he has seen or known of it, and the one who gave the testimony swore to confirm his testimony, and he had seen or heard the truth and did not correct the error with true testimony. In this case he is guilty, because he took part in the judgment against an innocent person, so he offers a sin offering.

entries.section: (1) Examples of sins and the necessity of confession

paragraphs.text: Creeping things: crawling insects.
Hidden from him: he did not know.

The second sin is if he touches the carcass of a wild beast or a cattle or an insect, or the body of a man, or anything of his uncleanness, such as the belongings of the leper (ch. 13) or one who has an issue or a woman with an issue of blood (ch. 12), and he did not notice it. This one also offers a sin offering.

entries.section: (1) Examples of sins and the necessity of confession

paragraphs.text: Pronouncing with his lips: uttering.

The third sin is if a person is hasty and swears, whether to do good to another or to do him harm, and he did not know that what he swore by conflicted with one of God's commandments and His law, and then someone informed him of this error into which he had fallen, so he needs to offer a sin offering.

entries.section: (1) Examples of sins and the necessity of confession

paragraphs.text: Confess: to admit his error.

In the three preceding cases, the offender should confess his error before the priest, offering a ewe or a female goat as a sin offering as explained before (ch. 4). This shows the importance of the Sacrament of Confession before partaking of the sacrifice of Christ on the altar, that is, His most holy Body and Blood.

Beware of rushing into speech or action lest you fall into sin... Listen well and pray to God and seek the counsel of your father of confession as much as you can, and God will protect you from many sins.

entries.section: (2) The sin offering for those who are not able

paragraphs.text: The poor man offers two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and their choice is as a symbol of purity and meekness, as explained before (ch. 1:14-17). And since it is difficult to separate the fat from the flesh in birds, one of them is taken in place of the fat and is burned entirely, so it is called a burnt offering although it is a sin offering, and the second, in place of the flesh, is the priest's portion for him to eat of it, so that the one who offers it is assured that his sacrifice has been accepted and his sin forgiven, and so that the priest may learn to accept the gift of the poor man however small, because he is the servant of the poor and the rich.
And the wringing off of the head without dividing it asunder is because it is written of Christ that not a bone of Him shall be broken.

entries.section: (2) The sin offering for those who are not able

paragraphs.text: Ephah: a grain measure with a capacity of 23 liters.

The one who cannot afford to buy the two doves may offer a small quantity of fine flour as a sin offering. But to distinguish it from the grain offering mentioned in (ch. 2), he does not put oil or frankincense on it, which are put on the grain offering and signify the work of the Holy Spirit and prayer, because the flour here does not signify the life of Christ on earth but bears the sin of the sinner. The priest burns a handful of it, and it mingles with the blood of the sacrifices on the altar and becomes a sin offering mixed with the blood necessary for forgiveness to take place, and the priest takes the rest as food for himself.

God welcomes my repentance and does not want to place on me a material burden that would hinder me from it, because He has no pleasure in the death of the sinner, but that he return and live. So what hinders me from practicing a life of repentance? However great my weakness or the difficulty of my circumstances, I can with God's help repent, and God accepts my return to Him even with a short prayer and a confession before the father of confession.

entries.section: (3) The trespass offering for an error directed against God

paragraphs.text: Estimation: evaluation.
Shekel: a unit of weight.
Shekel of silver: a silver coin weighing one shekel.
Shekel of the sanctuary: an exactly accurate shekel kept in the sanctuary, whose weight is double the ordinary shekel.
This is the fifth sacrifice, and it points to the work of Christ in forgiving our sins directed against God, and it is of two kinds:
1- Trespass against God and His temple and His holy things.
2- Some grave trespasses against men, which also include trespass against God, as in (ch. 6; ch. 14:12; ch. 19:20).....

In these verses it speaks to us of sins directed toward God, and the value of the ram of the sacrifice is determined by the priest according to the harm that has come upon God's holy things. The priest also determines the value of the appropriate compensation, apart from the value of the sacrifice, and the fifth part of the value of the harm is added to the preceding, to remind a person to sanctify his five senses that were defiled by the trespass, so that he does not sin again by them.

The trespass here is referred to as being through ignorance, because the Lord's ordinances are many and a person may be unaware of some of them. And the error in the holy things of God is either through ignorance in fulfilling His law, such as not offering the silver for the firstborn or not offering the firstfruits and the tithes, so the priest estimates the amount that should have been offered to God and adds a fifth to it, and he gives it to the priest, and he also offers a ram to make atonement for him.

entries.section: (3) The trespass offering for an error directed against God

paragraphs.text: Trespass: transgression against the rights of God.
Trespass: transgression or violation or guilt.

Among the examples of the Lord's prohibitions against which a person may trespass: eating of the parts of the sacrifice of which eating is not permitted (ch. 22:10-14), or using an animal that has been vowed to God (Deut 15:19). The sacrifice here is mentioned before the compensation because the error is directed against God, who does not give priority to material things. It is noted in the trespass offering that it is a ram and not a ewe, because the price of the ram is higher, for trespass is graver than sin because it is directed to God, so a more costly sacrifice is offered to show the heinousness of the sin.

If you sin, repentance is not enough, but compensation for the damages of the error is necessary, otherwise being content with repentance would carry laxity and an escape from the consequences of sin.
The trespass offering and the laws of the sacrifices

entries.section: (1) The trespass offering for an error toward others

paragraphs.text: Lie: deny.
That which was delivered him to keep (a found thing): belongings that fell from one person and another person found, picked up and took.

The trespass here is directed against a person, but it also contains a breaking of God's commandments, so because of the gravity of this sin the Law counts it a trespass and not an ordinary sin, and it is such as:
1- Theft of a deposit: if a person places money or belongings with another, and the other afterward denies that they are with him and takes them for himself.

2- Theft of a trust: such as robbing minors of their rights by their guardians, and dishonesty in buying and selling, or the dishonesty of the worker in the perfection of his work or exaggeration in demanding his wage, and likewise the reverse: the employer's reducing the worker's wage and delaying giving him his wage.
3- Robbery: what is meant is stealing from others in secret and then denying what was stolen.
4- Seizure: what is meant is theft by compulsion and refusal to return what was stolen.
5- Taking a found thing: a person takes what he finds on the road or in any place, though it is not his own but belongs to others, and then denies that he took anything, and even swears to it.
The word "unwittingly" is not mentioned, because the rights of people are clear.

Here we notice that a person's spirit and body and all his abilities are a trust from God, and we are stewards over them to use them for His glory, so it is not right for us to seize them for ourselves and use them for our own passions and base desires.

Likewise the faith delivered to us and all the teachings of the Church are a trust from God, and we are bound to teach them accurately to others and not to add to them or change them according to our own ideas.

The trespass offering signifies Christ's taking away our trespasses on the Cross, even in the hardest sins, for He bore all our sins directed toward Him or toward our brothers, mankind, and He gives us this justification in the sacraments of the Church.

entries.section: (1) The trespass offering for an error toward others

paragraphs.text: In the principal: at its original value.

Here it mentions compensation by returning in full what was taken, at its value, before offering the sacrifice, because repentance is not accepted before the wrong is put right. And the addition of a fifth is compensation for the one who suffered the harm, since he suffered distress that was not only material but psychological; it is compensation for the psychological pain, and so that the wrongdoer may feel his wrong, in addition to offering the sacrifice while asking God's forgiveness.

entries.section: (1) The trespass offering for an error toward others

paragraphs.text: The priest determines the value of the ram that is offered according to the measure of the sin that he committed against God, and he makes sure that this trespass occurred in its five cases mentioned before, lest it be a false accusation, and the ram is offered as a trespass offering so that God may forgive him.

Be faithful with the rights of others, so give them to them before you take your own rights, and if you borrow something from a person, return it. And be careful of the feelings of others, so do not wound anyone with condemnation or mockery, but honor all, and God will bless you and honor you.

entries.section: (2) The law of the burnt offering

paragraphs.text: Hearth: the top of the bronze altar.

Here it speaks of some of the laws concerning the burnt offering mentioned in (ch. 1), and it begins by speaking of the daily burnt offering that is offered in the evening, so that the priests may learn the order of offering every sacrifice. The burnt offering remains burning on the altar from six in the evening, the time of offering the evening burnt offering, until the morning. It signifies the Christian who remains aflame with the love of God throughout the darkness of this age until the dawn of eternity.

entries.section: (2) The law of the burnt offering

paragraphs.text: Breeches: part of the priestly garments; they are short trousers worn under the clothes.
The priest puts on his priestly garments, which are of white linen, in order to take up the ashes of the burnt offering (Ex 28:

40-43), and this shows the value of these ashes, which point to the body of Christ after His death on the Cross, for it is a place of the delight of the Father's heart because He endured pain to the end. Then the priest takes off his priestly garments, in which he may not go outside the tabernacle of the congregation, and puts on his ordinary clothes and carries the ashes of the burnt offering to a holy place surrounded by a wall outside the camp called the place where the ashes are poured out, that is, the place where the ashes are thrown (ch. 4:12). This is so that no one may tread on them or they be scattered in the air, since they are the remains of a holy sacrifice, just as we now honor the tomb of Christ.

entries.section: (2) The law of the burnt offering

paragraphs.text: The holy fire is not put out on the altar by night or by day, for the priests arrange the wood in the morning and lay the morning burnt offering on it at a time when the remains of the evening burnt offering are still burning with fire, in addition to the fire's burning with the various sacrifices.

The fire had come down from heaven at the anointing of Aaron and his sons as priests and kindled the burnt offering laid on the altar (Lev 9:24), and this fire continued until the Babylonian captivity, and then it returned in the days of Nehemiah from the well in which it had been hidden (2 Macc 1:19-36).
The fire on the altar points to the fire of the Holy Spirit, which is never extinguished in the Church forever and works in it and in its sacraments.

Often our love for God grows cold in periods of lukewarmness, but prayer makes the Holy Spirit return and always kindle in us this fire. So take care of your prayers and your reading in the Holy Bible every day, that the Holy Spirit may work in you and you may be comforted and reassured.

entries.section: (3) The law of the grain offering

paragraphs.text: The priest offers the grain offering before the altar and takes a handful of its flour and its oil for God, while the frankincense, which represents prayer and worship, is taken entirely for God and burned on the altar. The handful of flour that the priest took signifies the Incarnation of Christ, who took hold of us and brought us near to the Father.

entries.section: (3) The law of the grain offering

paragraphs.text: Leaven: leavened bread.
Most holy: set apart for the priests only.

The remainder of the grain offering is set apart as food for the male priests, for the male signifies spiritual manhood and striving, and this points to Communion, which only the strong strivers enjoy. They eat it in the house of the Lord because of its holiness, just as the Body and Blood of Christ are now eaten in the Church. The grain offering is to be unleavened, that is, without leaven in it, because leaven signifies evil. It is noted that the Body of Christ in the Church is leavened, since Christ bore our sins on the Cross and died for us and removed from us the punishment of sin, which leaven signifies. The rest of the grain offering is eaten by the priests, as they eat the remainder of the sin offering and the trespass offering after the fat is offered on the bronze altar.

entries.section: (3) The law of the grain offering

paragraphs.text: The grain offering is holy food, so it sanctifies and blesses the one who eats it, and it signifies the grace of God given in the Sacrament of the Priesthood. And everything that touches this food is sanctified, such as the vessels in which the food is put, which are set apart for this and nothing else is eaten in them.

As for the portion of the priests from the peace offerings and the crops and the fruits offered as firstfruits, it is of a lower degree of holiness, so the whole family of the priest is permitted to eat of it, males and females, and this is in a holy place and not in the house of the Lord as with the preceding foods.

entries.section: (3) The law of the grain offering

paragraphs.text: The priest would offer daily, with the morning burnt offering and the evening burnt offering, an offering as mentioned in (Ex 29:40), which is:
1- A tenth of an ephah of fine flour mingled with oil.

2- A fourth of a hin of wine (see the explanation in the commentary on Ex 29:38-42). For the priest too, as a man, needs to offer an offering, that is, he needs the grace of Christ. The priests would offer this offering at their consecration only, but the high priest offered it daily to show his great need of divine help. The offering of half of it in the morning and half in the evening shows the priest's constant need of God, so he offers with the morning burnt offering a tenth of an ephah of fine flour and with the evening burnt offering a tenth of an ephah of fine flour also, as the Book of Exodus shows, and the priests would offer this offering on the day of their anointing, that is, after the completion of their anointing as priests.

entries.section: (3) The law of the grain offering

paragraphs.text: Fried: mixed and mingled.
Baken pieces: small pieces of bread.

The grain offering of the priest is offered like the ordinary grain offering, on a metal baking pan and mixed with oil, which signifies the Holy Spirit. The grain offering is a symbol of the life of Christ on earth, who was anointed with the Holy Spirit at His baptism. The grain offering is broken into pieces to declare that Christ was pure on the outside and on the inside also, for the breaking into pieces signifies the showing of the inside.

entries.section: (3) The law of the grain offering

paragraphs.text: The anointed high priest offers the grain offering in place of Aaron after his death, for it is the ordinance of the high priest, whether Aaron or the one who succeeds him.

entries.section: (3) The law of the grain offering

paragraphs.text: Every offering of the priest is burned and none of it is eaten, as an indication of the priest's being wholly consecrated to the service of God, whereas of the grain offering for the people a part is offered on the altar and the rest is eaten by the priest.

Ask God's help, if you are a father or a mother or a servant, that He may give you grace in caring for those around you, so that God is the One working in you and through you and influencing the souls of those whom you shepherd.

entries.section: (4) The law of the sin offering

paragraphs.text: The sin offering is slaughtered in a holy place on the north side of the bronze altar, where the burnt offering is slaughtered (ch. 1:11), because by the redemption of Christ our sins were taken away and He gave us holiness. The fat of it is offered on the altar and burned, and the rest is eaten by the priest in the house of the Lord, so that the one who offers the sacrifice is assured of the removal of his sin by the burning of part of his sacrifice on the altar and the eating of the rest of it by God's priest.

entries.section: (4) The law of the sin offering

paragraphs.text: The sin offering signifies Christ, so the priest receives blessing and holiness when he eats of it, and its blood that is sprinkled on his garment is washed in a holy place to confirm its holiness.

entries.section: (4) The law of the sin offering

paragraphs.text: When one of the people offers a sin offering, its fat is burned and the flesh is eaten by the priest.

If he cooks these parts in an earthen vessel, it must be broken, because it has absorbed some of its holy blood and has become holy, so it is broken and not used again for ordinary foods because it is holy and it is thrown in a clean place. But if the vessel is of bronze, it is enough to scour it and rub it and wash it to remove the traces of the sacrifice that clung to the sides of the vessel and to cast them in a clean place.

entries.section: (4) The law of the sin offering

paragraphs.text: The ritual here is as explained before in (ch. 4), with the emphasis on not eating the sin offering if it is of the kind mentioned in (ch. 4:1-21), that is, offered for the sin of the priest or the congregation of the people, and likewise the two sin offerings that are offered for the high priest and then for the people on the Day of Atonement (ch. 16:11-15). That is, the sin offering whose blood is brought into the sanctuary is not eaten of at all but is burned entirely, whereas the one whose blood is not brought into the sanctuary is eaten by the priests and their male sons, and they eat it in the house of the Lord.
Reflect on the pains that our sins and uncleannesses cause our Lord Jesus Christ, the Holy One, so that you hate sin and no longer welcome it or seek to practice it.
Continuation of the laws of the sacrifices

entries.section: (1) The law of the trespass offering

paragraphs.text: The trespass offering is treated like the sin offering as most holy, because it shows that Christ is holy although He bore the sins of the whole world.

entries.section: (1) The law of the trespass offering

paragraphs.text: All the sacrifices are slaughtered in one place on the north side of the bronze altar to declare that they are all aspects of one sacrifice, the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, and to show its effect and its results in our lives, as mentioned in (ch. 5:14-19; ch. 6:1-7, 17). The two sacrifices are slaughtered in the same place before the Lord, that is, they bring the sinner back inside the house of God so that He is pleased with him. The blood is sprinkled round about on the bronze altar like the burnt offering, so its blood, which signifies the blood of Christ, bears the sins of the sinner for him, and the fat is burned in the same way explained before.

entries.section: (1) The law of the trespass offering

paragraphs.text: The priests and their male sons eat of the trespass offering as happens in the sin offering, so that the one who offers it may be assured that God has accepted it and removed His wrath from him.

entries.section: (1) The law of the trespass offering

paragraphs.text: The one who offers the sacrifice takes nothing of it, because it has taken away his sins, but the priest takes the skin as a second declaration to the one who offers it that God has accepted his sacrifice, and this reminds us of Adam, to whom God gave the skin to cover his nakedness and Eve's, and Adam was considered the priest of the family at that time.

entries.section: (1) The law of the trespass offering

paragraphs.text: After the priest offers a part of the grain offering on the altar, the priest who offered it eats the remainder of it, which is what is baked in the oven or the frying pan or on the baking pan, that is, while it is fresh. But the offerings mingled with oil and the dry ones are eaten by the rest of the priests and their male sons. The baked things given as a portion to the priests, the sons of Aaron, point to the word of God, which is the living spiritual bread that the priest feeds to his children by his teachings to them, and this word is characterized by five attributes that the ways of offering show:
1- Baked in the oven, that is, the fiery word of God issued by the power of the fiery Holy Spirit.
2- Dressed in the frying pan, that is, presented with deep and moving thought.
3- Dressed on a baking pan, that is, a word that reveals the mind of God to man and reveals the mind of man before God.
4- Mingled with oil, that is, accompanied by the power of the Holy Spirit as in the grain offering.
5- Dry, as in the offering that accompanies the sin offering, because sin dries up a person's spiritual life.
Thus the priest receives, as Christ receives, the sweet fruits of his children as he receives the dryness of their bitter life, to lead them in every case on the road of salvation.

Take care to teach your children the way of God and to care for each one individually, supporting him in his weaknesses and developing his gifts, so that you bind him to the love of Christ and he remains steadfast in the Church.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: The peace offering is of three kinds:
1- The peace offering for thanksgiving (vv. 11-15).
2- The peace offering for a vow (v. 16).
3- The peace offering for a freewill offering (vv. 16-18). And offered with the peace offering:
A - An unleavened grain offering, which includes:
1- Unleavened cakes mingled with oil.
2- Unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
3- Fine flour mingled with oil and fried, that is, well mixed, and made into cakes.
Of these three kinds some is taken and offered on the altar, because all are unleavened and so signify the pure life free of the evil that leaven signifies.

B- Leavened bread is offered with the peace offering to be eaten with this sacrifice, and none of it is offered on the altar, as God stipulated in (ch. 2:11), and this leavened bread also signifies Christ, who bore our sins and then passed through sufferings and death, that is, the fire.
These three kinds, that is, the sacrifice and the unleavened and the leavened, are offered as thanksgiving to God for His love and His gifts.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: Heave offering unto the Lord: lifted up before God and given to the priest.

The priest takes for himself one of each kind of food offered with the peace offering, and burns the fat of the sacrifice on the altar and sprinkles its blood around it. The priest's taking of the offerings means, for the one who offers the sacrifice, that he has given God something of his offering, and then the one who offers it eats the rest.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: The day of his offering: the day of offering the sacrifice with the baked things.

The one who offers the sacrifice eats the rest of the flesh on the same day of its offering when it is offered for thanksgiving, that is, none is left until the next day. The first reason is care that the flesh not spoil, and the second is that what is left over is for the poor, because what remains overnight will be burned. This signifies spiritually the necessity of not postponing the immediate enjoyment of the Lord and thanking Him for His gifts, and likewise the necessity of not leaving anything of the Body and Blood of the Lord in the Liturgy until the next day.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: Voluntary offering: voluntary and not obligatory, that is, a sacrifice offered out of love for God, and it is other than the vow, which is connected with a particular request. If the animal offered as a voluntary offering is lost, it is not replaced, whereas in the case of a vow replacement with one like it is required.
The peace offering may be offered either as a vow to God or as an offering of love to Him. In this case it is permitted to eat of it on the first day and the second day of its offering.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: What remains of the flesh of the voluntary offering or the vow on the third day is burned with fire, so that it may not be exposed to spoiling, and on the other hand so that it may be an encouragement to the one who offers the sacrifice to let the poor share in eating of his sacrifice. It is permitted to eat this sacrifice in the tents of its owners.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: It shall be an abomination: the sacrifice offered becomes unclean on the third day.

The soul .. shall bear his iniquity: the one who offered it sinned and needs to offer a sacrifice so that God may forgive him. The one who breaks God's law and eats on the third day of the peace offering, the following happens to him: 1 - His sacrifice is not accepted.
2- The flesh left until the third day becomes unclean and makes unclean the one who eats it.
3- The one who eats of this flesh and becomes unclean sins and needs to offer a sacrifice so that God may forgive him.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: Here it stresses two conditions for dealing with the peace offering, which are:
1- The necessity of burning the flesh of the peace offering if it touches anything unclean, and no one eats of it.
2- The one who eats of the peace offering must be clean, that is, with no uncleanness in him such as an issue of blood from him (ch. 15:19).

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: If a person, man or woman, is so bold, while having an uncleanness, whether an issue in a man or an issue of blood in a woman (ch. 15), and eats of the peace offering in violation of God's law, he is cut off from the congregation of the children of Israel and loses his membership and his belonging to the people of God, because he made light of God's law and did not feel his uncleanness and cleanse himself from it. This signifies persisting in sin and then coming forward to partake of the Holy Mysteries, and whoever does this needs severe repentance.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: If the person is not unclean in his body as in (v. 20), but he made light of it and touched an unclean person or an unclean beast, such as the carcass of a beast or any unclean animal as the Law prescribes (ch. 11:13), then for his making light he is separated and cut off from the people of God.
And the touching of uncleanness signifies mixing with the wicked or listening to the teachings of those who have left the Church.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: God forbids His people to eat the fat of the animals offered as sacrifices, because the fat is set apart for God, so it is not right to trespass upon God's rights, and this signifies the offering of the tithes and the firstfruits to God and not falling short in them.
And they may eat the fat of other clean animals of which they do not offer to God, such as gazelles. Likewise the fat mixed with the flesh of the animal of which sacrifices are offered to God.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: Dead animals and beasts of prey are not offered as sacrifices and are not eaten, but their fat may be used in any works that a person needs, such as lighting.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: If a person is so bold as to eat of the fat of the sacrifice offered to God and trespasses upon His rights, he is cut off from the people of God, because he defies Him and breaks His law, and the elders of the Jews used to rule that he be whipped 39 stripes if he ate unwittingly, but if he ate deliberately he is cut off as the Law prescribes.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: He also warns against eating blood as explained before (ch. 3:17), and the one who eats of it is cut off from the people.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: Wave: he moves it to the east and the west and the north and the south.

The one who offers the sacrifice carries on his hands the breast and the right shoulder while sitting before the priest, then he stands before the priest, and the priest places his hands under the hands of the one who offers the sacrifice to lift them with him and move them in the four directions, east and west and north and south, before God.

The lifting up of the breast and the right shoulder, that is, offering them to God, and the priest assists him in that, while the waving of them, that is, moving them toward the four directions, is a declaration that God is present everywhere and is the Controller of all, so he offers this sacrifice to Him.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: After the priest burns the fat of the sacrifice to the Lord on the altar, he takes the breast, and it becomes the portion of all the priests who are in the house of the Lord.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: The right shoulder: the right front leg.

The right shoulder is given to the priest who offers the sacrifice, for it is a heave offering to God who dwells in the heavens, and the priest takes it, so the one who offers it feels that God has accepted a peace offering.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: This is God's ordinance throughout the generations, that the breast of the sacrifice and the right shoulder be given to the priests to eat, so that the one who offered the sacrifice feels that God has accepted his sacrifice. On the other hand, God provides food for His priests who are consecrated to His service, and there is a relationship of love between the priests and the people.

entries.section: (2) The law of the peace offering

paragraphs.text: This is also what happens on the day of the anointing of the priest, that is, his being set apart and established as a priest, so the shoulder of the heave offering is given to him and the breast to the priests, as we mentioned in (vv. 30-34), and this is his portion of the peace offering throughout the generations.

God concludes His words about the laws of offering the sacrifices mentioned in the first seven chapters of this book, declaring that this is what God commanded Moses on Mount Sinai when He gave him the laws of the sacrifices.

The ritual of the consecration of the priests (1) The consecration of the priests (vv. 1-13:) 1 And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, 2 Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and a bullock for the sin offering, and two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread; 3 And gather thou all the congregation together unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. 4 And Moses did as the LORD commanded him; and the assembly was gathered together unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. 5 And Moses said unto the congregation, This is the thing which the LORD commanded to be done. 6 And Moses brought Aaron and his sons, and washed them with water. 7 And he put upon him the coat, and girded him with the girdle, and clothed him with the robe, and put the ephod upon him, and he girded him with the curious girdle of the ephod, and bound it unto him therewith. 8 And he put the breastplate upon him: also he put in the breastplate the Urim and the Thummim. 9 And he put the mitre upon his head; also upon the mitre, even upon his forefront, did he put the golden plate, the holy crown; as the LORD commanded Moses. 10 And Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that was therein, and sanctified them. 11 And he sprinkled thereof upon the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all his vessels, both the laver and his foot, to sanctify them. 12 And he poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron's head, and anointed him, to sanctify him. 13 And Moses brought Aaron's sons, and clothed them with coats, and girded them with girdles, and put bonnets upon them; as the LORD commanded Moses.

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Moses prepared everything according to the command of God, who chose Aaron and his sons for the priesthood. And all the people were present before the tabernacle to rejoice in the ordination of their priests.

Moses was a priest, or the middle stage between the head of the family being its priest and the setting apart of the priesthood in particular persons for the whole people, namely Aaron and his sons. God declared this in the Psalm: "Moses and Aaron among his priests" (Ps 99:6). Moses brought Aaron and his sons and all the people to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation for their ordination to take place there, for the following reasons:
1- So that the people may know that their ordination is from God and by His command, and not a private idea of Moses out of love for his brother Aaron.
2- So that the people may feel the majesty of the priesthood and respect it and submit to it.
3- So that Aaron and his sons may feel their responsibility for the care of all the people of God gathered in their multitudes during the ordination.
Moses brought the requirements of the ordination, which are:
1- The garments of the priesthood that Aaron and his sons would wear, mentioned in (Ex 28, 39).
2- The anointing oil that Moses prepared, mentioned in (Ex 30:22-33).
3- The animals to be slaughtered, which are a bull and two rams; the explanation of the ritual of offering them will come in this chapter (Ex 29).
4- A basket with unleavened bread in it; the explanation of the ritual of offering it will come in this chapter (Ex 29).

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: The faithfulness of Moses was manifested in his conveying precisely what God says to the people.

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Washed: washed thoroughly.

The washing of the priests is a reference to the two sacraments of Baptism and Confession, which wash a person from his sins, for before the servant calls people to repentance he must first repent himself. The washing is a cleansing of the body from the outside in preparation for a great matter, the ordination to the priesthood, and it signifies purity of heart so that Aaron and his sons may serve God without any personal ends and shepherd His people in purity.
This ritual continues in the New Testament, for the priest washes his hands during the Liturgy for the same purposes mentioned before.

Moses completed the washing of Aaron and his sons in a special place of the tabernacle of the congregation, because it was a washing of the whole body, and not in the laver in which they would afterward wash their hands and feet before entering the sanctuary.

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Moses brought the priestly garments that are mentioned in detail in (Ex 28) and put them on Aaron and his sons, and these garments point to the attributes and work of Christ as mentioned in the commentary on the Book of Exodus (Ex 28). These garments signify:
1- The greatness of God and the dignity of serving Him.
2- The importance of adorning ourselves with virtues to be children of God.
3- The importance of purifying the heart and being clothed with righteousness when we stand before God.
4- The splendor and majesty of the priesthood.
5- These garments signify the garments of light that the children of God wear in the Kingdom (Rev 4:4).

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Then he anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it and the priests themselves with the anointing oil, as a reference to the sanctification of the servants by the Holy Spirit, just as He descended on Christ in the waters of the Jordan to begin His ministry (Mt 3) and on the Church on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2). Thus the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation and likewise the priests became set apart for the service of God and not for any other work.
And the sprinkling of the oil seven times on the bronze altar signifies the perfection of sanctification, and it is done by sprinkling the oil with the finger seven times.

And the pouring of the oil on the head of Aaron, so that it ran down upon his beard and his garments, unlike the anointing of the priests on their foreheads with this oil, is because of the greatness of the responsibility of the high priest, who is responsible for the care of the priests and all the people.

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: After Moses had clothed Aaron with his garments and anointed him, he clothed the priests with their garments, mentioned in detail with all their meanings in (Ex 28).

The angels stand with reverence and purity and concentration of mind before God, praising Him at all times; so also should the priests and servants be during their service. So when you stand to pray or offer the service of God, humble yourself and fix your gaze on Christ and set aside all your concerns to enjoy being in His presence.
