entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the head of the bull, confessing their sins, so that this bull may bear their sins for them, and it is a symbol of the blood of Christ, which cleanses everyone who believes in Him, for it is necessary for the salvation of all, whether the common people or the priests. Then the bull is slaughtered and Moses smears the blood on the horns of the bronze altar and pours out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. We notice here that the one who performs the priestly work is Moses, and they do not enter with the blood into the sanctuary, because the priests have not yet been ordained.

Then Moses burns the fat on the altar, while the skin of the animal and the rest of its flesh and its waste are burned outside the camp and no one eats of them, because it is a sin offering for the priests, as passed in (ch. 4).

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Then he offered the burnt offering for them, a ram, according to the ritual explained before in (Ex 29:

15-18), to show that Christ, who died on the Cross in obedience to the Father, fully satisfied divine justice, so that God was pleased with humanity in Christ. By this Aaron and his sons declare their readiness to please God and to offer their whole lives to His service.

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: The third offering and sacrifice was the second ram, which is the ram of "consecration," and consecration means the filling of the hand, and the spiritual purpose of it is that the servants should not come forward to the service of God with empty hands and life, but full of the fruits of the Spirit.

What is meant by the sacrifice of consecration is the beginning of the priest's service, that is, the sharing of Aaron and his sons in offering the sacrifice to God. It resembles to some extent the peace offering, with some differences that will appear in the explanation of the following verses.

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: The tip of the ear: the lower part of the outer ear.
Thumb, great toe: the big finger of the hand or foot.

After Moses slaughters the ram of consecration, he anoints the ear and the thumb and the great toe of the right hand and foot of Aaron and his sons, and this signifies the opening of the ear to hear and understand the word of God, and the sanctification of the hand for doing His pleasure, and the readiness of the feet to walk in His way. Then the blood of the sacrifice is poured out and the fat burned, as explained before in (Ex 29:19, 20).

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: He offered to the Lord an unleavened cake and a cake of bread and a wafer, after waving them before the Lord, as a declaration that He is the source of all grace by His pure life like the unleavened, and satisfying like the bread, and gentle like the wafer, as explained before in (Ex 29:23-25). And Moses put this unleavened bread and wafer with the fat and the right shoulder on the hands of the priests and waved them before God and then burned them on the altar.

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Then he waved the breast and took it as a portion for himself as the servant of the sacrifice, as explained before in (Ex 29:26).

entries.section: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

paragraphs.text: Moses sanctified Aaron and his sons and their garments with the anointing oil and the blood of the sacrifice, in a clear reference to the work of the Holy Spirit (the anointing oil) and the blood of Christ for the sanctification of man. And he gave them their portion to eat on the same day and to burn what is left over (Ex 29:21, 31-34).

Before you speak to people about God or advise them about anything, take care of your personal relationship with Him in repentance and prayers and reading in the Holy Bible, so that you are strengthened by the grace of God and your words are effective with those who hear you.

entries.section: (3) The duration of the completion of the consecration of the priests

paragraphs.text: The days of your consecration: the days of your ordination and consecration.
The Lord has commanded to do: that is, the ritual of the first day is repeated for the seven days.

The ritual of ordination extends to the completion of seven days, as a pledge that the consecrated servant will spend his whole life, the period of his sojourn on earth, in the service of God without turning back. And God promises him that He will supply his need and fill his hand with provision and good all the days of his life. In the New Testament the priest spends forty days after his ordination in retreat and worship in preparation for service throughout his life.

And Aaron and his sons remain inside the house of the Lord these seven days, taking care not to enter the sanctuary because their ordination has not been completed. The rituals of ordination that took place on the first day, of washing and offering the sacrifices and the food, are repeated each day of the seven days.

entries.section: (3) The duration of the completion of the consecration of the priests

paragraphs.text: God warns the priests through Moses not to go out from the house of the Lord for seven days lest they be punished with death, and this is as a symbol of the consecration of their lives to God, so that they do not do the works of the world, otherwise they become as dead in the sight of God. In these seven days they complete the worship of God and the rituals of ordination.

entries.section: (3) The duration of the completion of the consecration of the priests

paragraphs.text: Aaron and his sons obeyed and carried out everything that God commanded.

Our consecration to Christ by Baptism and the Holy Myron has made us His servants throughout the whole of our lives. We serve Him with all our energies and He is responsible for us and for all our needs; this is our way as Christians in our lives.
God's acceptance of the sacrifices

entries.section: (1) Sacrifices for the priests and the people

paragraphs.text: Moses brought Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel on the eighth day of their ordination. It signifies eternal life after the present time with its seven days, and the eighth day is the beginning of their service after the completion of their consecration. And he called the elders as representatives of the people.

entries.section: (1) Sacrifices for the priests and the people

paragraphs.text: Moses no longer offered the sacrifices after the consecration of Aaron and his sons, and the priests began to offer from their own means for themselves a sin offering as an expression of their personal repentance and their confession of their error and their need of the cleansing blood of Christ, and then a burnt offering as an expression of the consecration of their lives, so that their obedience to God becomes complete (ch. 4, 1). The scholars of the Jews think that this sin offering was an atonement for the sin of making the golden calf. In general, the repetition of offering sin offerings, since they offered a sin offering during their ordination, expresses:
1- That the sacrifice of blood does not give complete forgiveness, whereas the sacrifice of Christ gives complete forgiveness.
2- Their constant need as human beings for the forgiveness of their sins, which occur throughout their lives.

entries.section: (1) Sacrifices for the priests and the people

paragraphs.text: After the priests offered sacrifices for themselves, they offered sacrifices and offerings for the people, that they too might be cleansed, because they had shared in the worship of the golden calf in addition to the rest of their sins.. The following is noticed in the sacrifices and offerings:
1- They begin with a sin offering, which is a kid of the goats, because it is not possible to stand before God except after getting rid of sin.

2- Then the offering of a burnt offering, which is a calf and a lamb of the first year, that is, each of them a year old, which signifies maturity and at the same time innocence, and it means the consecration of the heart to God, as the sacrifice is burned entirely on the altar.
3- After getting rid of sin and declaring the consecration of the heart to God, fellowship with Him is possible, so they offer a peace offering, which is a bullock and a ram.
4- In the end they offer offerings which are fine flour mingled with oil, as a declaration of offering all their possessions to God and of their seeking His blessing in their lives.
With this preparation they are able to meet God and enjoy the sight of Him.

entries.section: (1) Sacrifices for the priests and the people

paragraphs.text: Moses and the priests took the sacrifices and offerings to the front of the tabernacle of the congregation and went in with them before the bronze altar, and with them were the representatives of the people, that is, the elders, for the offering of the sacrifices and offerings. And Moses said to them that the offering of these sacrifices is the condition of preparation for meeting God.

entries.section: (1) Sacrifices for the priests and the people

paragraphs.text: The horns of the altar: that is, the altar of incense inside the sanctuary.
The bottom of the altar: that is, the bronze altar.

Aaron began by offering the first sacrifice, which is the sin offering for himself and for his sons the priests, and he slaughtered it at the side of the bronze altar on the north, and took some of the blood and anointed the horns of the altar and poured out the rest at the bottom of it.

entries.section: (1) Sacrifices for the priests and the people

paragraphs.text: Then he offered the fat of the sacrifice and burned it on the bronze altar, while the skin of the animal and all its flesh he burned outside the camp.
