The law of the issue: introduction:

In this chapter he speaks of the man from whose reproductive organs semen flows in a diseased manner for a number of days, and also of the natural emission in physical relations. He also speaks of the flow of blood from the reproductive organs of the woman in the normal state, that is, the monthly period, and also in the diseased state, which continues for longer periods. All of the above is considered uncleanness, and he provides the cleansing and treatment particular to each case. God cares about these matters and counts them as uncleanness in the Old Testament for the following reasons:

1- With the Fall of man, sin spread in the human race and all became condemned to death, and the means of producing offspring is the reproductive organs; therefore what comes out of him is considered unclean, because it produces children born in sin.
2- The issue signifies a lack of discipline in material desires, so God alerts us to be scrupulously careful so that He may protect us from falling into various desires.

3- The aspect of health, that is, care for the cleanliness of these organs for the sake of propriety. This last meaning is what remains in the New Testament, after Christ lifted the sentence of death by His redemption, and the uncleanness was removed.
(a) The issue of a man (vv. 1-18:) which includes two cases:
God spoke to Moses because he was the prophet, the leader of the people and the receiver of the Law, and likewise to Aaron because he was the high priest responsible for applying the Law.

The first case is the emission of semen from the organs of the man (he spits), whether continuously or emitted for a period and then stopping (being stopped up), and it may return to flowing again. These are the symptoms of the disease of the issue, whose sufferer is considered unclean. This signifies carelessness and lack of discipline.

The uncleanness is not limited to the one with the issue, but also everything he sits or lies on, whether a bed, seats or any physical thing, which also becomes unclean. This signifies the transmission of evil from the wicked person to those around him, so that we may keep away from everything that relates to sin or leads to it.
God warns against approaching the one with the issue or what belongs to him and what he uses, for all these things are unclean, and He specifies them as follows:
1- The bed on which the one with the issue lies. The two signify laziness and carelessness.
2- The furniture, that is, the seats and belongings on which the one with the issue sits.

3- Whoever touches the body of the one with the issue --< signifies clinging to the unclean. The Law tries to keep us away from every appearance of uncleanness, so a person must care, by his own will, for his purity in all his dealings with those around him.
And if a person becomes unclean through any of the above, he must do the following:
1- He washes his clothes, as a symbol of the cleansing of his conduct.
2- He bathes, as a symbol of the purity of his inner being.

3- He remains unclean until the evening, as a symbol of remembering the seriousness of uncleanness so as to guard against it. The unclean person refrains from eating of the peace offerings or taking part in the religious feasts so that he may be careful afterward, because the clean person enjoys drawing near to God in every way.

A clean person may be made unclean against his will when the one with the issue spits on him, whether he does not intend it or whether he is wicked and does it in contempt of this clean person. In both cases the clean person becomes unclean because unclean spittle fell on him. This signifies a warning against anything that comes from the unclean, for their words and deeds are unclean and must be avoided.
And the remedy, if this clean person becomes unclean, is that he do as in the previous cases, that is, wash his clothes, bathe, and remain unclean until the evening.

Likewise everything on which the one with the issue rides, whether an animal or any equipment placed on the animal such as the saddle (the packsaddle), is unclean, and everyone who touches or carries it becomes unclean. This signifies the use of the means of evil that the unclean use.
And the remedy is that the one who became unclean bathes, washes his clothes, and remains unclean until the evening.
The one with the issue must wash his hands before touching any person; if he does not do this and touches someone, he makes him unclean. This signifies clinging to the wicked.
And the remedy is that this unclean person washes his clothes, bathes, and remains unclean until the evening.
The vessels that the one with the issue touches become unclean, and they are of two kinds:
1- Cheap vessels such as earthen vessels, which must be broken and disposed of.

2- Expensive vessels such as those made of wood and metal, which are rinsed with water. This signifies that sin defiles the place and everything connected with the sinner, and that by washing, that is, repentance and prayer, everything is sanctified; but any physical thing that causes stumbling must be disposed of, such as unclean pictures or films.
The cleansing of the one with the issue is carried out in the following steps:
1- Seven days must pass after the issue has stopped, to confirm that the issue will not return.
2- Washing his clothes.
3- He bathes, that is, washes his body in running water, that is, flowing water like the water of rivers, not pools or marshes.

The fourth step in the cleansing is done by the cleansed one with the issue seven days after the issue has stopped. He goes to the priest and offers two turtledoves or two young pigeons, that is, two small doves, because the meat of an old pigeon does not taste good and one must offer God the best; but the turtledove tastes good whether it is old or young. The priest kills one of them and burns it entirely on the altar, so it is a burnt offering, while the other he kills as a sin offering and the priest eats it (as mentioned in ch. 1:14-17). Thus the one with the issue completes his purification.

Take care not to cling to the wicked and all their places, their means of evil and their way of life, lest you be swept along with them into evil. And in proportion to your striving, be confident that God will support and protect you so that you keep your thoughts, your words and all your conduct in purity.
Seed of copulation: the emission of semen from the man, which by uniting with the ovum in the woman establishes seed or offspring. What is meant by copulation is that it takes place during sleep.

If a natural issue, not a diseased one, comes from the man when he is asleep, whether accompanied by dreams or not, he becomes unclean. This was so in the Old Testament because offspring or seed was born bearing the sin of Adam and Eve, before redemption was accomplished and we received salvation through Baptism. So the overflow of semen was considered unclean, and the one to whom this happened bathes all over and remains unclean until the evening.
Likewise every garment of cloth or leather on which a person is lying and on which this fluid falls becomes unclean and needs to be washed, and remains unclean until the evening.
The second natural case is the emission of semen in marital relations; the man and the woman must bathe and remain unclean until the evening.

In the New Testament, these natural things are no longer unclean, because redemption has been accomplished; but for the sake of propriety and cleanliness, washing is required, and Communion is not permitted, because these cases are considered a breaking of the fast, whether the emission of fluid is connected with evil dreams or with physical relations, so abstaining from such relations is required before Communion.

Physical relations within marriage are an expression of love and for the sake of begetting good offspring, but abstaining from them for the sake of Communion is good and necessary, because the aim of marriage is not sex; rather, it is a means of expressing love, and the spouses use it in the measure suitable for them and abstain from it for God's sake before Communion and during the fasts as much as they are able.
(b) The issue of a woman (vv. 19-33)

Here he speaks of the flow of blood from the woman's body in the case of the monthly period, which is the natural issue, and the woman is considered unclean for seven days. What is meant by seven days is a period sufficient for this flow to end, which usually lasts four or five days but does not exceed seven days. The woman is considered unclean in the Old Testament because the blood that comes out of her is connected with the production of the ovum, which unites with the sperm and produces offspring who bear the sin of Adam and Eve. In the New Testament it is not considered uncleanness, because Christ has accomplished redemption and gives us salvation in Baptism and the sacraments of the Church.
And everyone who touches the woman in her state of menstruation, that is, the flow of blood from her in the monthly period, becomes unclean.
Every bed on which this woman lies or place on which she sits during menstruation becomes unclean.
Everyone who touches the bed or belongings of the menstruating woman becomes unclean, and must bathe and remain unclean until the evening.

Here he refers to the things that are placed on the bed or on the seats on which the menstruating woman sits; these things become unclean by being placed on the bed or belongings, and whoever touches them becomes unclean until the evening. Here he affirms that uncleanness is transmitted from the unclean person to everything physical connected with her. And the one who touches these things does not need to bathe, because they were merely placed on the bed or belongings.

This is an unusual case, namely a husband lying with his wife while he does not know that she is menstruating, nor does she know either, that is, the flow of blood begins during or shortly before the marital relation, and this union took place unintentionally. The man too becomes unclean for seven days like the woman, and during the seven days in which he is unclean he makes unclean every bed on which he lies.

But if he knows that his wife is menstruating and lies with her deliberately, they are both cut off from the people of God for their carelessness, though they knew of the uncleanness, and for their boldness in having physical relations (ch. 20:18). All this signifies the importance of being scrupulous in keeping away from evil and uncleanness.

Although Christ has lifted the uncleanness from the woman in this period, yet for the sake of cleanliness and propriety it is not fitting for her to partake of the Holy Sacraments. Let this period be an opportunity for repentance over her sins, when she feels some pain and remembers God's judgment of old on Eve, pain in childbirth, a little of which appears during the monthly period. Let it be an opportunity for greater self-examination, prayer and reading of the Holy Bible, so that she may enjoy Christ who gave her salvation and purity.

Here he speaks of the flow of blood in a diseased manner, which is not limited to the flow of blood during the period of menstruation but extends for many days, or flows at other times than the period of menstruation; this makes the woman unclean. The diseased bleeding, that is, that which has no relation to menstruation, is considered uncleanness, because blood means life and its shedding signifies the death that came upon humanity after the fall into sin. But through the redemption of Christ the sentence of death was lifted, and consequently the uncleanness when blood flows; therefore a woman who bleeds because of a disease in the New Testament is considered clean, but she does not partake of the Holy Sacraments because of impropriety; yet in special cases, when the duration is long, she may partake with the guidance of the father of confession.
Because the woman with the issue is unclean, everything she lies or sits on becomes unclean.
Everyone who touches the woman with the issue, or what she sits or lies on, becomes unclean, and needs to bathe and remain unclean until the evening.

After the flow of blood stops, the woman waits seven days to be sure that the issue will not return again, and then she goes to the priest with two turtledoves or two small doves, and the priest offers one of them as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and makes atonement for her, and she obtains her purity, as mentioned in the interpretation of (vv. 14, 15).

God commands Moses and Aaron to teach the people all these laws mentioned in this chapter, so that they may keep their purity and be able to draw near to the house of the Lord and His holy things, and so that they may be protected from death because of breaking the Law of God and falling into uncleanness.
Here he declares that this chapter contains the laws of cleansing for the woman and the man with an issue, of both kinds.

Use bodily weakness and sickness to humble yourself before God and ask for His help, and increase your prayers, readings and meditations, so that you may experience fellowship with Him in a new depth.

The Day of Atonement: general introduction:

The Day of Atonement is the greatest of the feasts of the Jews. On it atonement is made for the sins of the high priest and all his people and for everything in the tabernacle of the congregation. It signifies Good Friday, on which Christ offered atonement and salvation for the whole world, for everyone who believes in Him.

It is the only day on which a human being enters the Holy of Holies, namely the high priest, who signifies Christ, who by His redemption gave us salvation and brings us into the Kingdom of Heaven. On this day all the people fasted in humility over their sins, which God removes and for which He makes atonement by the sacrifices that signify Christ. And on this day the high priest takes off his splendid priestly garments and puts on the ordinary linen garments of the priests, so as to approach the service of this day in humility, just as Christ carried His Cross in humility on this day for our sake.

This feast falls on the tenth day of the seventh month, followed five days later, on the fifteenth day, by the Feast of Tabernacles. Because of the greatness of the Day of Atonement, it is called the Sabbath of Sabbaths, that is, complete rest. The chapter mentions the rites performed on this day, while the additional sacrifices offered on this day are mentioned in the Book of Numbers (ch. 29:7-11), and the duties performed by the people on this day are mentioned in (ch. 23:26-32). The rites particular to this feast are summarized in:
a- Preparation for the feast:
1- The high priest leaves his dwelling and stays in a room next to the temple or in a tent beside the tabernacle of the congregation to prepare for the rites of the feast.

2- The elders of the Sanhedrin, that is, the supreme council of the Jews, recite to him the rites of this feast throughout the seven days so that he may know them perfectly, because he will perform some of them alone inside the Holy of Holies.
3- During these seven days the high priest carries out the priestly service in the tabernacle of the congregation, such as offering the sacrifices and lighting the lamps inside the sanctuary.
4- On the night of the Day of Atonement the high priest does not sleep, and the priests stay around him so that he may be careful lest he have a dream by which his body would be made unclean.
b- The rites of the feast:
They include four stages:
The first stage: the morning sacrifice (Ex 29:38-42, Num 28:3-8)
1- The high priest bathes and puts on his splendid priestly garments (Ex 28).
2- He commands the priests who assist him to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and clean it in preparation for the service of this great day.

3- He slaughters and offers a lamb of the first year as a burnt offering, and with it one tenth of flour mingled with a fourth part of a hin of oil, and pours a fourth part of a hin of wine on the sacrifice (Ex 29:38-42), as is customary every morning in the tabernacle of the congregation. But the difference today is that the one who offers the morning sacrifice is the high priest himself, and it is doubled if the Day of Atonement falls on a Sabbath (Num 28:9, The second stage: the service of atonement:

This is the service particular to the Day of Atonement, in which the high priest enters the Holy of Holies four times, while on the rest of the days of the year he never enters it. The rites are summarized as follows:
1- The high priest takes off his splendid priestly garments and washes, and then puts on priestly garments of linen like the rest of the priests (v. 4).
2- He lays his hand on the head of the bull that will be slaughtered as an atonement for his sins and the sins of the priests, confessing his sins and theirs, for he is their representative.
3- He casts lots on the two goats presented as an atonement for the people, so that one of them is offered as a sin offering and the other for Azazel (vv. 7, 8).
4- He slaughters the bull at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation and puts its blood in a vessel inside the sanctuary.

5- He takes the censer and the incense dish, fills his hands with incense, and enters the Holy of Holies for the first time. He places the censer on a stone inside the Holy of Holies and puts plenty of incense in it, so the place is filled with incense, which covers the Ark of the Covenant, so that the high priest does not see it and does not die, for because of the greatness of the Ark it is not right for anyone to see it (vv. 12, 13). He leaves the incense inside the Holy of Holies so that the cloud of incense continues to cover the Ark and its cover.
6- He takes some of the blood of the bull and enters for the second time and sprinkles it on the cover of the Ark seven times, as an atonement for his sins and the sins of the priests (v. 14).
7- He lays his hand on the goat of the sin offering and slaughters it at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and puts its blood in a vessel inside the sanctuary.

8- He enters for the third time into the Holy of Holies with the blood of the goat of the sin offering, offered for the sins of the people, and sprinkles some of it on the cover of the Ark seven times.

9- He mixes the blood of the bull with the blood of the goat of the sin offering and sprinkles it on the contents of the sanctuary, then goes out from it and sprinkles it on the rest of the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation to make atonement for it (vv. 17-19).
10- He gives the second goat, alive, to a man to let it go in the wilderness for Azazel (vv. 20-22).
11- He commands that the bull and the goat of the sin offering be burned and their ashes cast outside the camp.
12- He takes off his linen garments and washes, and then puts on his full priestly garments, that is, the splendid ones.
13- He offers two rams as a burnt offering to God at the feast, one for himself and the other for the people.
The third stage: the additional sacrifices, which are mentioned in (Num 29:7-11), for himself and for the people, and which include:
1- A bull as a burnt offering, and with it three tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and half a hin of wine, which he pours on it when offering it.
2- A ram as a burnt offering, and with it two tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and a third of a hin of wine.
3- Seven lambs of the first year as burnt offerings, and with each one of them one tenth of fine flour mingled with oil and a fourth part of a hin of wine.
4- A kid of the goats as a sin offering.

The fourth stage: the evening sacrifice (Num 28:8), which is offered every evening by the same rite as the morning sacrifice mentioned in the first stage. The difference on this day is that the high priest is the one who offers it, not the priests.

After the death of the two sons of Aaron, "Nadab and Abihu," who offered strange fire on the altar of God and not the holy fire that came down from heaven (ch. 10), the Lord spoke to Moses and gave him the law of the great Day of Atonement, on which Aaron the high priest would enter the Holy of Holies to make atonement for himself and for the people.

God warned Aaron, by the mouth of Moses, against entering the holy place, meaning the Holy of Holies, and passing the veil, which is the curtain dividing the sanctuary from the Holy of Holies, and standing before the mercy seat, that is, the cover of the Ark of the Covenant, where God appears in His glory in a cloud, whether what is meant is the natural cloud that appears in the sky or the thick incense that Aaron offers before the Ark of the covenant of God, so that its appearance is like a cloud. The high priest's entry into the Holy of Holies takes place once every year, on the Day of Atonement. If he enters at any other time, he dies, out of respect for the presence of God and as a showing of His justice, which cannot be seen except through the blood of Christ, which is offered only on the Day of Atonement before the Ark of the Covenant.

The fear of God protects you from falling into many sins, and if you fall, you hasten to repentance. If God in His love allows you to see His temple and His altar and to partake of His Holy Mysteries, do not forget His justice and the fear of Him, so that you may pray with reverence and live in purity.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

paragraphs.text: Here he mentions the sacrifices that Aaron offers for himself and for the priests, which he buys from his own money, as a declaration that all need the redemption of Christ, whether priest or people. These sacrifices that he prepares are:
1- A young bullock, which he offers as a sin offering to make atonement for his sins and those of the priests.
2- A ram for the burnt offering, that God may be pleased with him and the priests.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

paragraphs.text: After Aaron has offered the morning burnt offering as set out in (Ex 29:38-42, Num 28:3-8), he goes to a place in the tabernacle of the congregation to wash his whole body and to change his splendid priestly garments for garments like those of the rest of the priests, which are:
1- Linen breeches, which are an undergarment worn on the waist and covering the thighs.
2- A linen coat, which resembles a long robe reaching to the feet and covering the arms.
3- A linen girdle, which is a belt tied around the waist with its two ends hanging down in front toward the feet.

4- A linen miter, that is, a cap, which is a simple head covering like what the priest wears today (the tailasan). The high priest changes his garments and puts on ordinary priestly garments so that he may be humbled and know that he needs atonement to be made for him like the rest of the priests and the people.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

paragraphs.text: As for the sacrifices that Aaron offers for the people, which are from their own money, they are:
1- Two kids of the goats as a sin offering; one is slaughtered and the other is let go, as we will explain in this chapter, and they are to make atonement for the sins of all the people.
2- A ram for the burnt offering, that God may be pleased with the people.
3- Additional sacrifices mentioned in (Num 29:7-11).

entries.section: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

paragraphs.text: Aaron brings near the bullock of the sin offering, which he will offer for his sins and those of his sons the priests, and stands it before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation at the bronze altar, and confesses his sins and those of his sons the priests before God, that He may forgive them, in a general confession that was written down among the Jews. The priest of the New Testament too, in the Divine Liturgy, offers repentance for his own sins before the sins of the people, which is a declaration of the need of all for the salvation of Christ the Redeemer.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

paragraphs.text: The high priest stands the two goats offered for the sins of the people before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, with their faces toward the west, that is, toward the sanctuary, and casts lots between them to choose one of them for the Lord, that is, to offer it as a sacrifice to God, and the other for Azazel, that is, to let it go far away outside the camp into the wilderness. The first goat signifies the shedding of the blood of Christ for the forgiveness of the sins of those who believe in Him, and the second goat signifies Christ's removal of our sins from us and setting them far away, that is, freeing us from them, for the word Azazel comes from separating and removing. The goat to be offered as a sacrifice is tied with a red thread, and the goat of Azazel with a scarlet thread, that is, a dark red, to distinguish them.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

paragraphs.text: Aaron presents the goat of the sin offering that will be slaughtered before God, and slaughters it after slaughtering the bullock.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

paragraphs.text: As for the second goat, on which the lot fell to be for Azazel, the high priest stands it before God to make atonement for the people, that is, to bear their sins and remove them by sending it to Azazel, as a symbol of separating the sins of the people from them.

If Christ has redeemed you by His blood and has removed your sins from you, and you have received this in the two sacraments of confession and Holy Communion, then take care to live pure and reject all sources of evil.
Aaron himself slaughters the bullock of the sin offering, because by it he makes atonement for himself and for the priests his sons.

Aaron takes the golden censer particular to this day, which is large in size, and puts in it burning coals, that is, glowing charcoal from the bronze altar, and enters the sanctuary and takes his hands full of sweet incense beaten small, that is, well ground so that it burns easily and its sweet fragrance spreads, and puts the incense in a special golden vessel. It is noted that he took a large quantity of incense to put in the large censer, so that the incense would spread inside the Holy of Holies like a great white cloud covering the Ark of the Covenant and the mercy seat, so that Aaron does not see it, because it is the great throne of God, which no one can look at because of its greatness and the fear it inspires. Then he enters the Holy of Holies carrying the censer in his right hand and the incense vessel in his left. He enters sideways, that is, not looking toward the cover of the Ark, and places the censer on a stone set on the ground, and then puts into it the abundant incense that is in the vessel, so the incense rises like a mist and covers the whole place, and he senses the presence of God and cannot see the mercy seat.

Aaron goes out from the Holy of Holies to the sanctuary and takes the vessel containing the blood of the bullock from one of the priests assisting him, and then enters the Holy of Holies a second time and sprinkles with his finger, that is, sprinkles some of the blood, on the cover, which is called the throne or the mercy seat, and at which the two cherubim, who represent divine justice, look. This blood signifies the blood of Christ, which fulfills the requirements of divine justice on behalf of mankind and so saves us.

Then he sprinkles some of the blood that is in his left palm with the finger of his right hand on the ground before the Ark, as a declaration that we have no entrance to the Father except by the blood of Christ the Redeemer (Eph 2:18). He sprinkles toward the east side of the Ark of the Covenant and the cover, which faces the veil and the sanctuary, because the place of the Holy of Holies is to the west of the sanctuary and to the west of the tabernacle of the congregation. So Aaron enters from the veil, that is, from the east, toward the Ark of the Covenant that is in the west, so that the east side of the Ark is in front of him, and he sprinkles on it; thus the phrase "toward the east" means the east of the Ark.

Wonderful is God in His humility; around Him the angels stand in great fear, yet He condescends to dwell in our midst so that we may take courage and draw near to Him, and He makes atonement for us by His blood so that we may be accepted, indeed loved and brought close to His embrace. May we offer repentance with reverence, so that we may enjoy His love and live in reassurance.

Aaron slaughters the goat on which the lot fell and offers it to God, takes some of its blood and enters the sanctuary and then the Holy of Holies, and sprinkles some of its blood once on the cover and seven times on the ground before the Ark, as he did in the rite of sprinkling the blood of the bullock. This time he offers the blood on the cover to make atonement for the people, and on the ground so that the people may have access and entrance to God, that He may be their God and they may be His people. This is the third time that Aaron enters the Holy of Holies.

Because of the sins of the people, the house of God, that is, the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation, is defiled; therefore he mixes the blood of the bullock with the blood of the goat and sprinkles it on all the contents of the sanctuary, and likewise the contents outside the sanctuary, so the tabernacle of the congregation is cleansed, for the blood of Christ cleanses His people and His Church. This shows that our sins defile the Church of God and anger Him, but by faith and repentance we obtain our purity.

Because of the people's defilement of the tabernacle of the congregation, there is an opinion that the seven times that the priest sprinkles before the Ark on the ground are to cleanse the Holy of Holies, which became unclean because of the sins of the people, and then he sprinkles on the rest of the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation so that the whole place may be clean.

While the high priest is entering the Holy of Holies, there is no one, of the priests or the people, either in the sanctuary or in the tabernacle, since all need atonement to be made for them. And Aaron here signifies Christ, by whom alone atonement is made for us.

Here he stresses the sanctification of the contents of the sanctuary and the tabernacle, and in particular the altar of incense, which is in front of the veil, that is, in front of the Holy of Holies. He takes some of the blood of the bullock and the blood of the goat, mixed together, and anoints the four horns of the altar, and then sprinkles with his finger seven times on the altar, to declare that Christ the Redeemer, by His blood and ascending as incense for us before the Father, is our strength, which appears in the horns of the altar, which represent strength, and seven times, that is, the fullness of sanctification and cleansing. And just as he cleansed the altar of incense, he cleanses the rest of the contents of the tabernacle by sprinkling them with blood.

After finishing the sanctification of everything in the tabernacle of the congregation by means of the blood of the bullock and the goat, he brings the second goat, which is called the goat of Azazel, and stands it before God at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, that is, he declares that it is presented to God.

Aaron comes forward as the representative of the people and lays his hands on the head of the live goat, that is, the goat of Azazel, and confesses the sins of all the people in a prayer that the Jews had prepared to declare their repentance and ask God's forgiveness. This is a clear symbol of the sacrament of confession, in which the sins of those who confess are transferred to Christ, who bears them for them and forgives them. Then he gives this goat to the one he meets, which is either the first person he meets or a particular person who comes forward and meets Aaron, and this is the more common opinion; this person is most likely one of the priests, and he takes the goat and goes with it to the wilderness and lets it go alive there.
The following is noted about the two goats:

1- The slaughtered goat is a symbol of Christ who died on the Cross for us, and the second goat, which is let go alive in the wilderness, is a symbol of the risen Christ who gave us new life by the Resurrection.

2- The first goat makes atonement by its blood in the sanctuary, far from the eyes of the people, while the second goat is let go alive before the eyes of all, to reassure them that their sins have been forgiven. The first is a secret relationship with God, and the second is a public relationship and visible worship before all.

Drive away your evil thoughts by repeating the Psalms or occupying yourself with anything spiritual. It also helps you to change your place, to declare before God your rejection of the evil thought, so that He supports you with His help to cut sin off at its roots and stop its growth into any other forms in word or deed.

After the high priest lets the goat of Azazel go, he enters a special place in the tabernacle of the congregation and takes off the simple linen garments in which he offered the sacrifices and offerings of atonement, and then washes his whole body, as an expression of his purification from the sins connected with the sacrifices and offerings of atonement; then he puts on his full priestly garments, that is, the splendid ones, to offer the additional sacrifices of this day, followed by the evening sacrifice.

After the high priest bathes and puts on his full garments, he offers burnt offerings for himself and for all the people. For after sins have been removed by the sacrifices and offerings of atonement, he can offer burnt offerings of a sweet savor before the Lord, who is pleased with him and with his people.
These burnt offerings are:
1- A ram as a burnt offering for Aaron, mentioned in (v. 3).
2- A ram as a burnt offering for the people, mentioned in (v. 5). In addition to the additional burnt offerings mentioned in detail in (Num 29:7-11), which are:
3- A bull, and with it three tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and half a hin of wine, which he pours on it when offering it.
4- A ram, and with it two tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and a third of a hin of wine.
5- Seven lambs of the first year as burnt offerings, and with each one of them one tenth of fine flour mingled with oil and a fourth part of a hin of wine.
In addition to a sin offering, which is a kid of the goats.
Aaron offers the fat of the sin offering, which is:
1- The fat of the bullock that Aaron offered as an atonement for himself (v. 3).
2- The fat of the sacrificed goat offered as an atonement for the people (v. 5).

3- The fat of the goat of the sin offering offered as an additional sacrifice and mentioned in (Num 29:10, 11). The altar mentioned here is the bronze altar that is in front of the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, on which the fat of the sacrifices is offered because it is the richest part of them, and so it is offered to God.

The goat of Azazel is considered unclean because it bears the sins of the people; therefore the one who takes it and lets it go in the wilderness must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and remain outside the camp until the evening to be cleansed and be permitted to enter the camp.

Offer repentance for any sin you fall into, or any stumbling place you go to, or any clinging to wicked people who helped you toward sin, and let there be for you a period of repentance, that is, prayers and confession, so that you may be permitted to partake of the Holy Sacraments.

In the case of any sin offering, after its fat is offered, the priest eats its flesh and takes its skin. But on the Day of Atonement, because the sin offerings are offered for the priests themselves and for all the people, no one eats of the flesh of the sin offerings, whether the bullock or the goat offered for the people or the additional goat; rather, they bring out the flesh of these sacrifices, their skins and their dung, and burn them outside the camp, just as Christ was crucified and suffered outside the camp.
The one who burns the flesh, skin and dung of the sin offerings outside the camp becomes unclean because they bear sins, and therefore he must:
1- Wash his clothes.
2- Bathe his body.
3- Remain outside the camp until the evening, and then enter it after he has obtained his purity; this is like the one who let go the goat of Azazel.

After that the high priest offers the evening burnt offering as is customary every day, by the same rite as the morning burnt offering that was offered at the beginning of this day, as mentioned in (Num 29:12).
God concludes His words about the Day of Atonement by asking the following of His people:
1- Humbling themselves and repenting of sins, which is accompanied by fasting.
2- Freeing themselves from material work to concentrate on the meaning of atonement.
3- Observing the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month every year until Christ came and accomplished atonement for our sins on the Cross.

4- All the worshipers receive forgiveness of their sins on this day, whether the native, who is of Jewish origin, or the stranger, that is, the Gentile who became a Jew and lived with the children of Israel.

He mentions that the Day of Atonement is a day of rest, so he calls it a sabbath, that is, a day of rest, but it need not fall on a Sabbath; it can be any other day of the week. Along with rest, he stresses the necessity of fasting, which he expresses as humbling oneself before God.

The high priest anoints the one who will succeed him, who is his firstborn, as high priest after him, and he is the most important person on this day because he himself offers the sacrifices, assisted by the rest of the priests. He fills his hand, that is, he offers the sacrifices and carries them with his hands, and takes care to wear linen garments as a declaration of his humility, as we mentioned.

The high priest sanctifies and anoints everything in the tabernacle of the congregation with the blood of the sacrifices of atonement, as a symbol of Christ, who sanctifies His Church and all who believe in Him.
Moses and Aaron obeyed all the commands of the Lord, and so they kept the Day of Atonement every year.

The Church offers special worship on Good Friday every year and offers fasting and humility on the Friday of every week, so it is an opportunity for you to remember the mercies of God, who removed your sins by His redemption, so that you thank Him, praise Him and contemplate His love.
The altar and the blood
The Lord spoke to Moses, the leader of the people, to instruct Aaron and his sons, so that they might understand and teach the people the manner and the place of slaughtering the sacrifices.
There are two opinions in the interpretation of these two verses:

1- That the talk here is about the children of Israel slaughtering animals for food while they are in the wilderness of Sinai, so they bring their sacrifices and slaughter them before the tabernacle of the congregation. But when they moved to the Promised Land, many of the tribes came to live far from the tabernacle of the congregation or the Temple of Solomon, so they slaughtered in their cities what they needed to eat (Deut 12:20-22). What was slaughtered for food in the wilderness was little, since they depended for the most part on eating the manna, as is shown by the fact that they asked God for meat and He gave them quail (Ex 16:12); consequently, their coming to the tabernacle of the congregation to slaughter what they would eat seldom happened.

2- What is meant here is what is offered as sacrifices to God, that is, peace offerings, and it is required that the sacrifices be offered in one place, the tabernacle of the congregation, and whoever does not do this is put to death. This word of God is of great importance, for these reasons:
1- Keeping them away from the worship of idols and from slaughtering to them, so that worship is offered to God alone.
2- Attachment to the house of the Lord, where they bring all their requests.
3- Adherence to one rite in offering the sacrifices, to establish one set of spiritual thoughts.
4- Unity among the people, since all offer their sacrifices in one place.
5- Giving the priests a portion of the sacrifices as their food.
6- Giving the Lord a portion of their sacrifices, that He may bless their lives.

So everyone who wants to slaughter, whether inside the place where the tents of the children of Israel are or outside it, must come to slaughter before the tabernacle of the congregation, and whoever slaughters in another place is counted as a shedder of blood or a murderer and must be put to death. But there are some scattered events in the Holy Bible in which sacrifices were offered on special altars other than the altar of the tabernacle of the congregation, in obedience to orders from God and for spiritual purposes that God willed, as in the case of Gideon (Judg 6:25-27), Samuel the prophet (1 Sam 7:5-11), David the prophet (2 Sam 24:
18-25), and Elijah the prophet (1 Kgs 18:19-40).

These sacrifices, of which the people will eat, are what are called peace offerings, and the one who offers them takes care to offer the fat to God, which the priest lifts onto the altar, and likewise the blood is sprinkled around the altar, because the fat is the richest part of the sacrifice and the blood represents the life of the sacrifice, so they are offered to God, as the rite of the peace offering prescribes (ch. 3).

The Egyptians and some other countries offered sacrifices to animals such as the calf Apis, so God forbids them to offer sacrifices to the goats that they worship. These idolatrous worships were connected with fornication, so God warns them against them, and the offering of sacrifices is restricted to God alone at the tabernacle of the congregation.
Know that you are wholly consecrated to God, so do not give your thoughts or your time to the world and to evil, so that your effort may be spent on the love of God and the love of others.

God stresses that all the sacrifices or burnt offerings offered to God are to be at the tabernacle of the congregation and not in any other place. This applies to the Jew or the non-Jew who has joined the people of God and believed in Him and wants to offer a sacrifice.
God forbade His people to drink blood, for the following reasons:
1- Because blood represents the life of the animal, which belongs to God and not to a human being.
2- The blood is offered on the altar to God, as it signifies the blood of Christ, who makes atonement for us.

This applies to the children of Israel or the strangers dwelling among them, and whoever breaks this commandment is cut off from the people, that is, he is set apart from it and loses his membership in the people of God because he treated His commandments lightly.

Do not make light of the commandments of God and justify your errors, lest God abandon you and you lose His blessing in your life; and know that all God's commandments are for your good, so do not be drawn after the pleasures of your sinful self.

If they hunt an animal of the clean animals that are permitted to be eaten, but which is not of the kind that is offered as sacrifices to God, such as deer, then when they slaughter it to eat it, they must pour out its blood and drain it and then cover this blood with dust, for the following reasons:
1- Out of respect for the blood, which represents the life of the animal that God created.
2- Because the animal, like man, is made of dust and returns to dust.
3- Lest the blood be used in offering it to idolatrous worship.

He also warned them not to eat an animal that was torn by a wild beast or died in any accident, because a large part of its blood is still in it. Whoever knows that the animal is dead or a prey and eats of it, that is, insists on breaking the commandment, is cut off from the people of God.

If a person of the people of God eats of an animal that died or was torn by a wild beast and did not know this, and thought it was an animal slaughtered in the ordinary way, he becomes unclean for two reasons:
1- Because he drank blood retained inside the prey.
2- Because he ate flesh that the unclean beast had touched.
So he must bathe and wash his clothes and remain unclean until the evening, and whoever does not do so is punished according to the judgment of the elders of Israel.
Forbidden marriages and sexual perversions: general introduction
In the first ten chapters, the Book of Leviticus showed the hideousness of sin, which needed many sacrifices to make atonement for it, and these are aspects of the sacrifice of the Cross.
Then it presented practical laws on holiness in food and drink, clothing, dwelling and health in (ch. 11-15).
Then it presented the great Day of Atonement, which signifies the day of the Cross, and the law of slaughtering and the importance of blood (ch. 16, 17).
Then in the coming chapters it speaks about the importance of holiness in dealing with God and with others, and the holiness of the priests (ch. 18-22).
Before God gives them His laws of holiness, He declares to them that He is their God, and this means:
1- Their attachment to Him alone and not to the idol gods.
2- His love for them, His care for them and His concern for their holiness.
3- The fear of Him and adherence to His ordinances so that they are not punished.

God warns them against imitating the Egyptians in their idolatrous worships and customs, which they came to know during all their dwelling in Egypt. He also warns them against accepting the ideas of the Canaanite peoples, whom they will drive out and settle around them in the Promised Land, and against mixing with them and being defiled by their ideas. Rather, they are to hold fast only to the laws of God, their only God, and apply them and live by them and enjoy His care for them.

God's commandments are not mere orders; they give you a pure, happy life with Him. So take care to apply the words of the Holy Bible in your life, and do not be content with theoretical knowledge, so that you may taste fellowship with God through His living word in you.

Nakedness: the reproductive organs; what is meant by uncovering them is marriage and having physical relations. Here he warns against marrying close relatives. This was permitted before the Law of Moses, yet the Law of Moses is still applied in Christianity, and even increased in a few of its provisions, for the following reasons:
1- Preserving the purity of the feelings of fatherhood, sonship and brotherhood, apart from sex.
2- From the health standpoint, this is better for avoiding diseases and troubles that result in the offspring.
And God specifies these forbidden close kinships in the following verses.

He forbids marrying the father or the mother, or the father's wife or the mother's husband, because the two have become one flesh, and consequently the father's wife has become a mother and the mother's husband is a father. So to preserve the purity of the feelings and dealings of parents and children within the family, the Law forbade these marriages.

He also forbids marrying a sister, whether a full sister or a half-sister, of whom he said "born at home, or born abroad," that is, born of another mother or another father, in order to preserve the purity of the feelings and dealings of brothers and sisters together.
He also forbids a grandfather to marry his granddaughter, whether the daughter of his son or the daughter of his daughter, in order to preserve the purity of the feelings of fatherhood and sonship.

He also forbids marrying the daughter of the father's wife, because she is counted a sister like one born of the father, although she was born to the father's wife by another husband than the father; but by the woman's marriage to the father she became one with him, and consequently the woman's daughter is counted as his daughter, so it is not right to marry her.

He also forbids marrying the father's sister or the mother's sister, because she is a sister of the father or the mother and is very close, and is treated as a mother, so it is not right to marry her.

Likewise he forbids a girl to marry her maternal uncle or paternal uncle, or a son to marry the wife of his maternal uncle, for she is counted as his aunt, that is, his mother, so it is not right to marry her if her husband dies.

He warns against marrying the daughter-in-law, that is, the son's wife, for she is counted as a daughter. The punishment of one who marries or commits adultery with his son's wife was death (ch. 20:12).

It is also not right to marry the brother's wife after his death. But the Law of Moses permitted this marriage in one special case, namely if this brother had not begotten children before his death, so his brother marries her to raise up seed and the offspring are reckoned to the dead man so that he may inherit in the Promised Land (Deut 25:5-10). But in Christianity there is no longer a Promised Land but the heavenly Jerusalem, and consequently the Law forbids marrying the brother's wife after his death in all cases.
He also forbids marrying a woman and then marrying her daughter too, or her granddaughter, because by marrying the mother he became a father to her daughter and a grandfather to her granddaughter.

He also forbids marrying two sisters at the same time, because by this he makes them rivals and problems arise. But it is understood from this that marrying the wife's sister is permitted if the wife dies; in Christian law, however, marrying the wife's sister after her death is not permitted, because she is counted as his sister, in order to preserve the purity of dealings with the wife's sisters.

Let your love be pure, your look innocent and your dealings sound with your relatives. Do not be careless in the name of affection to the point of exposing yourself to attacks from Satan. And in proportion to your humility and care, you can live a life of strong, pure love for God's sake and be loved and useful to those around you.
God forbids physical relations with the wife during the period of her menstruation (the monthly period), for the following reasons:
1- She was considered unclean, so whoever approached her became unclean for seven days (ch. 15:19-24).
2- It causes diseases and bleeding, so relations at this time are against the woman's health.
3- It does not suit propriety, good taste and general cleanliness.
And whoever lies with a woman inadvertently becomes unclean for seven days, but whoever lies with her deliberately, both of them were cut off from the people (ch. 15:19-24).
Thy neighbour's wife: that is, his wife.
Seed: a physical relation that can produce offspring.
He warns against adultery because the Sixth Commandment forbids it (Ex 20), and whoever committed adultery was put to death by stoning (ch. 20:20, Deut 22:22).

Molech: the god of the Ammonites, also called Moloch or Milcom or Baal. He is the god of fire, and they offered him human sacrifices of their children, either by roasting them in fire or slaughtering them and then roasting them to please him, so they made them pass through the fire until they were burned, in order that he might be pleased with them.

He warns them against offering their children as sacrifices to Molech, because by this idolatrous worship they commit savage acts and declare their allegiance to the idol gods and their rejection of God, and so they profane His name.
Here he warns against sexual perversion, that a male lie with a male, and of course also a female with a female, for this is a great uncleanness.
Lie down thereto: an animal leaping upon a woman to have a physical relation with her.
He also warns them against being inflamed by their desires to the point of clinging to animals in order to have physical relations with them, for this is a great sin and uncleanness.

Take care in watching the various media so as not to defile your eyes and mind with the perverse practices of the world, and do not let curiosity draw you to this. It is not logical to desire these terrible evils, and leniency in seeing them may lead to attempting to practice them or justifying them, or at the least to defiling the mind.
I do visit: I repay.

God warns His people of the punishment that will come upon them if they fall into the preceding sins mentioned in this chapter, whether the perversions or the forbidden marriages. God will be angry with them as He will be angry with the peoples dwelling in Canaan, and will drive them out from before the children of Israel and settle them there in their place; if they sin, they too will be driven out of the land of Canaan, and this is what actually happened in the captivity, when they were driven out of their land and scattered among the kingdoms of the world because of their evils.
God calls His people to hold fast to His commandments and also to keep away from these sins mentioned before.

God makes clear that the pagan peoples defiled the land with the preceding evils, and if the people of God fall into them, they will defile the land and be exposed to the same fate as the pagan peoples, that the land will cast them out from it, that is, God will drive them out of it.
Ordinances: practices.
Rites: worship.

God declares that the souls that fall into these preceding sins will be cut off from the people of God and so lose His care, and may be exposed to death or other punishments; therefore He calls them to keep away from these perversions and evils and to hold fast to His commandments and His worship.

Look at the punishment of sin, which is eternal torment, so that you are not careless about the smallest part of it, however much the surrounding circumstances encourage you to it. Do not lose your eternity for these trivial and base things, and know that every striving or renunciation of anything that leads to sin is very precious to God, and He will help you, support you and compensate you with joys that cannot be expressed on earth or in heaven.
Worship and other laws

God requires His people to live in holiness because they are His children, and since He is perfect in holiness, they too must live in it because they are His children. They obtain this holiness through carrying out His commandments, which will be mentioned in the following verses, and through keeping away from the evils, some of which He mentioned in the previous chapter.

He requires every person to respect his mother and father, as the Fifth Commandment enjoined (Ex 20). Here he puts the mother before the father to declare the equality of the two in the eyes of the son and in the eyes of God, and because there may be a more affectionate relationship with the mother, yet it does not cancel respect and reverence, whether they are in their youth or in their old age; they give them adequate care and even honor them after their death.

He also reminds them of keeping the Sabbath day holy, as the Fourth Commandment enjoined (Ex 20), and likewise the seventh year and the year of Jubilee, that is, the fiftieth (ch. 25:4-12); this means respect for God and setting aside sufficient time for Him to worship Him.
He warns them against the worship of idols or making their images, for this is counted as a rejection of the worship of God.
The sanctuary of the Lord: the altar of God and His house.

If they slaughter peace offerings, of which they offer something to God and eat the rest, let it be eaten on the first and second day of the slaughter of the animal; on the third day this is not permitted, and whoever does so becomes unclean, and if he does so deliberately he is cut off from the people of God, because he wronged the house of God by not carrying out His commands, and this is in the case of a vow or a freewill offering, that is, an additional offering. But if it is a peace offering offered as thanksgiving to God, it is eaten on the day of its slaughter only (ch. 7:11-21).

Do you care for your parents and bear with them if they err? Know that honoring them rejoices the heart of God, because by this you declare your love for Him and for them, and also your humility, and so you receive many blessings.
Gleaning of thy harvest: what is scattered of the grain on the ground and gathered up.

Harvest, or gathering the crops, is a time of joy, so the Law reminds them not to forget the poor. The owner of the field should leave parts, even small ones, of his field in its corners, not reaping all that is in them, so that they may be for the poor to gather for themselves without embarrassment. Likewise what is scattered of the grain on the ground the reapers do not try to gather but leave for the poor and the strangers, that is, all the needy, to glean.
Thou shalt not glean it: do not gather the grapes from the field several times, but leave some of them remaining.
Every grape of thy vineyard: the scattered grapes that fell on the ground.

Likewise the owners of vineyards, when gathering the grapes, do not gather them several times but leave some of the berries on the vines for the poor to gather. And when some grains fall on the ground and are scattered, they leave them also for the needy. Here the Law gives several benefits, which are:
1- The owner of the field or vineyard feels the blessing of God, who stretches out His hand and takes a share from him through His poor children.
2- It fills the hearts of the owners of fields with mercy toward their needy brethren, so they feel their fellowship as one people of God.
3- The poor person does not feel embarrassment, but takes what he needs without asking.
4- Reducing or preventing begging, which troubles the rich as it troubles the poor.
The Law forbids some sins such as:
1- Stealing, whether by not returning a trust or by a person taking anything that is not his right.
2- Lying, to gain any gains or to hide a fault, or any deceit.

3- Dealing falsely, meaning treachery, whether by robbing rights or by any deceit, and it may reach murder as in Cain. And when he says "to his neighbour" he means deceit here, as a person finds treachery from one from whom he does not expect it; it is a wrongful exploitation of people's trust to achieve personal ends.

In the Old Testament God allowed His people to swear by His name so that they would not swear by the idol gods and so that their faith in Him would be strengthened, but He required the oath to be true, to confirm the absence of lying; and whoever swears falsely in the Old Testament wrongs the name of God and profanes it, because he used it in false speech. But in the New Testament, since the spiritual person has risen higher, he no longer uses the name of God in material dealings, as it is too lofty for that, so he does not swear at all.

He forbids employers to exploit or wrong those who work for them: they do not force them to do work beyond their strength or without pay, and they do not rob them of their rights by giving them less than their wages, exploiting their weakness and need, and they do not delay giving them their wages. Though they have the money with them, they delay the wages to the next day, although the hired servant or worker needs it today to meet his needs. That is, He forbids the strong man to use his strength in exploiting and wronging the weak.

He warns against exploiting the weakness of the helpless, such as the deaf, that is, one who does not hear, so we curse him, confident that he does not hear and cannot answer us; but his God, who allowed him this helplessness, hears and will take vengeance on us if we do not repent. Whoever wrongs a helpless person wrongs God, who allowed him this helplessness.

Likewise whoever puts a stumbling block in the way of a blind man, such as a stone or an obstacle, so that he trips and falls over it, God is very angry with him, so we must keep before us the fear of God and awe of Him, because He defends His helpless children and avenges them.

Here he addresses not only rulers and judges but every person, to judge with justice in all matters brought before him and not to wrong anyone, and to take care not to be deceived by the appearance of a poor man who looks weak but in truth has committed a crime; when his tears flow or he speaks in a low voice, this should not affect justice. On the other hand, do not pervert judgment and be lenient with a person of high standing, out of respect for him, acquitting him of a wrong he committed or wronging another.

What is meant by the talebearer is words of condemnation that wrong others, so the Law forbids carrying words of condemnation and spreading them, because it is a wrong against God, the Creator of those whom he condemns, besides a weakness of love toward them. He also warns against making light of the lives of others, which is represented by their blood, for example by not testifying to save them from death or danger, or leaving injustice to fall on them, or by bearing false witness against them or clearly wronging them; in this a person stands and tramples on the blood of his neighbor by his passivity.

He requires His people to love one another, and that no one carry hatred for anyone in his heart; and if someone wrongs another, let him go to him and rebuke him and admonish him (warn him), so that peace may return between them and he may always keep a pure heart toward everyone.

If any person of the people of God wrongs you, do not be angry with him and hate him and try to take revenge on him, but love him as yourself, because he is a member with you in the people of God, and every person of course loves himself and fears for himself. So one should love others as he loves himself, and have compassion on them if they err, and forgive them.
Gender: pair, mate.
God calls them to keep all His commandments, whether great ones or what seems small, as in the verse; all of them are important and have useful spiritual and material meanings.

So He forbids them to pair two kinds of animals, that is, not to carry out crossbreeding, and likewise not to sow the field with two kinds of crops, and also not to make their garments of two fabrics such as linen and wool, for the following reasons:
1- A person, if he mates two animals of two kinds and produces a new animal, may think that he is a creator and shares with God in divinity.
2- When two kinds are sown in one field, it is very hard to care for them together because of the differing needs for irrigation, fertilizing and harvesting.
3- Wearing garments of two fabrics may cause some troubles to the skin.

And the spiritual meaning of this is not to mix the thoughts of the world with spiritual thoughts, with the importance of concentrating on one spiritual thought, for example not being distracted during prayer by thoughts about service.
Bondmaid: a female slave.
Redeemed: her price is paid, that is, her redemption, to her owner, so that she becomes his possession and his maidservant.
Freedom given: her owner and master gave her to this suitor free of charge.

If a free man betroths a bondmaid and intends to pay her price so that she becomes his maidservant, but before he pays her price or her master gives her to him, he goes too far in playing with her until he commits adultery with her, the law of adultery, putting them to death (Deut 22:23), is not applied to them. This is because she is first the property of a master, and the ownership of this master must be respected and no loss caused him; and on the other hand, this man is her betrothed and intended to buy her so that she would become his wife like one of his concubines, that is, his maidservants whom he married. So the judges, that is, the elders of Israel, give them a sentence of discipline, most likely scourging.

After the discipline of the betrothed pair, the free betrothed man must offer a sacrifice for his trespass before God, which is a ram, because adultery is a grave sin directed against God even if the betrothed pair consented to this lying together. Here is a clear declaration of the need for the blood of Christ the Redeemer, whom this sacrifice signifies, for the removal of sin.
As for the betrothed bondmaid, because she owns nothing, she is exempted from offering the sacrifice and offers repentance only.

May you consider the feelings of others and not wrong them; put yourself in their place, and what you do not accept for yourself, do not do to them. And if you wrong them, offer repentance to God, apologize to them, and compensate them as much as you can for what they lost.
Uncircumcised: the tree is figuratively counted as uncircumcised, that is, not belonging to the people of God and not blessed by Him.
Uncircumcised: that is, not circumcised, and this meaning too is figurative, meaning that its fruit is not to be eaten.

This commandment concerns their life when they enter the Promised Land and plant a tree to yield fruit to be eaten, and this is of course apart from the trees planted by the original inhabitants of the land and apart from trees that do not yield fruit for eating. The commandment prescribes leaving the fruit for three years without eating of it, because the fruit of new trees is not fit to eat in the first three years, in addition to the fact that some pagan peoples offered the fruit of their trees at the start of planting to the idol gods, so their leaving these fruits declares their rejection of these idolatrous worships.
Before they eat of the fruit, they must receive the blessing of God, so they offer the fruit of the fourth year to God, and the priests and the Levites eat it.
In the fifth year and afterward they are permitted to eat the fruit, and it is blessed by God, and by this they declare their allegiance to Him and their enjoyment of His care.

Be careful to offer to God from your money and your various gifts, so that you may receive His blessing in your life, for a little blessed by God is better than much without blessing; and by this you also show your love for others.

He warns them against eating meat with its blood, that is, meat from which the blood has not been drained, out of respect for blood, which signifies the life of man, besides the fact that it stirs up the passions (ch. 17:14). The pagans used to dip meat in blood or drink it to please the gods.

He also warns them against imitating the pagans in optimism and pessimism, that is, being hopeful if they see or hear a sound and, on the contrary, expecting evil if they hear or see other things. All these are of course superstitions connected with pagan worships.
In addition to that, he warned them against divination, that is, searching for the future by astrology and various methods of charlatanry such as casting shells or asking sorcerers.

The men among some pagan peoples used to cut the hair of their heads round, leaving only a circle of hair on top of the head. Others tampered with the two sides of the beard, that is, the sideburns, cutting them and leaving a lower part around the chin. So God forbids them all these practices that the pagan peoples do to please their gods.

Some of the pagans, in excess of grief, used to cut their bodies as a sign of the loss of their hope and their loss on account of the departed one, so God commanded His people to keep away from this despair and its practices. He also commanded them not to make a mark, that is, marks by branding on the body, for the forms of some pagan gods, that is, to keep away from all pagan ideas.
Familiar spirits: evil spirits, that is, demons.

Wizards: evil spirits, since some think there are spirits that follow people and can harm them. He forbids them to believe in and seek the demons who take the form of familiar spirits or followers, and likewise those who deal with demons, who are called soothsayers; whoever contacts and deals with demons defiles himself and defies God, therefore He says "I am the Lord," that is, He warns them to fear. This is mentioned often in the Holy Bible, as in (Isa 8:19, Eph 5:11).

Do not be carried along with customs prevailing in society or widespread fears, lest you anger God in ignorance, for these are shadows of pagan worships. Rely on Him, confident of His care and His power, for He protects you so that you may live in peace.
He commands them to respect the elderly by standing before them until they allow them to sit down, for respecting the old man (the hoary head) is respect for God and the fear of Him.

He commands them to treat the stranger well and to love him like the ordinary citizen, indeed to love him as they love themselves. And to increase their sympathy toward strangers, He reminds them of the suffering of being a stranger that they endured in the land of Egypt, so that they may have compassion on strangers and treat them well.
Unrighteousness: injustice.
Ephah: a measure for grain equal to about 23 liters.
Hin: a measure for liquids equal to about 5 liters.

He requires them not to wrong others, not only in the judgments of the courts but in all dealings of buying and selling: they use just balances, and likewise the weights, that is, the metal pieces, are correct, not less when they sell or greater when they buy. Also the use of just measures such as the ephah and the hin, noting that there are correct standards in the sanctuary by which to check them.

God commands them to follow all His statutes and not to neglect any commandment, but to take care to apply it and not merely to know it, for the sake of the fear of God, who repeats His name "I am the Lord" sixteen times in this chapter.

If you feel God before you at all times, you will treat all people well and keep away from every sin, and if you err, you hasten to repentance and to apologize to others, and so you live in peace, pure and clean.
Punishments for those who violate the Law

God commands that anyone who offers one of his children as a human sacrifice to the god Molech, the god of the children of Ammon, out of fear of him, shall be put to death. This sin was mentioned in (ch. 18:21), but here the punishment is stated, which is death by stoning. This is carried out either by striking him with stones until he dies, or by binding him and throwing him down from a height onto a large stone and placing another large stone on his chest until he dies.

God declares His anger against the man who gave one of his children to the pagan god Molech, and decrees that He will destroy him, because by this deed he has defiled the sanctuary of God, which is His house and His people; that is, he has offended and defied God by this great evil.
If the clan of this wicked man cooperates with him and hides him, out of fear for him or of him, they thereby help him in his evil, so God declares that He will destroy him and destroy them.

Do not cover up sin, for by this you encourage it and make the wicked persist in it. Be strong and proclaim the truth, and care about the salvation of the souls around you; but present the word of God in the manner suited to the one to whom you present it, so that you may draw his heart to the fear of God and he may turn back from his evil.
Here God also decrees the punishment of whoever deals with mediums, sorcerers, familiar spirits and all who deal with demons: that he must perish and die. This sin was mentioned in (ch. 19:31).

Finally God commands them and warns them about the life of holiness in which they ought to live, because He is holy. If they are His people, they must be holy to Him, that is, they must not worship any god other than Him and must keep away from all pagan practices, and, on the other hand, they must keep His commandments and apply them in their lives.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: His blood shall be upon him: he shall be put to death.

The fifth commandment, as well as the Law (ch. 19:3), requires the honoring of parents. But whoever does not respect them, and instead dishonors them and insults them with cursing, does not respect God, nor those who are older than himself, foremost among whom are his parents; he has not appreciated their labors in his birth and upbringing. He is ungrateful, and therefore God commands that he be put to death.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: God declares the punishment for adultery with a married woman, which is death, carried out by stoning (Deut 22:22). But if she is a virgin, he marries her and pays a fine (Deut 22:28, 29). For adultery with a married woman is an assault on the oneness of the marriage and on the belonging of each to the other, whereas in the second case it is possible to marry her as a remedy for the wrong, and he is punished by paying a fine because he assaulted her and did not marry her like the other girls.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever dares to commit adultery with his father's wife must be put to death, whether he did this during his father's lifetime or after his death, because his father's wife stands in the place of his mother; he has assaulted motherhood and defied God.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever commits adultery with his daughter-in-law must be put to death, because he did not respect his fatherhood toward her, and through his lust he has set himself against God and against all values.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever falls into sexual perversion by having a physical relationship with a male has burned with his lust against all the natural laws that God created. He is like an animal in his lust and must be put to death.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: If a man marries a woman and her daughter at the same time, or marries the mother and then the daughter, or the reverse, that is, the daughter and then the mother, whether during the lifetime of both or after the death of one of them, he has assaulted motherhood by his marriage to the girl's mother, and daughterhood by his marriage to the mother's daughter, and so he must be put to death.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Their blood shall be upon them: there is no sin upon whoever kills them, because they deserve it.

This base sin, adultery with animals, was spoken of before in (ch. 18:23), and the punishment was the death of the man or woman who committed it, and of the animal, not because the animal had sinned, but to be rid of every trace of evil and uncleanness.

If you have sinned by adultery in any form, whether in word or deed, in any manner, do not be content with repentance, confession and Holy Communion alone. Keep away also, as far as you can, from everything associated with the sin, from persons and places, and get rid of any pictures or belongings that remind you of the sin, so that you begin a new, pure page with God.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: Whoever marries his sister, whether his full sister or his half-sister, is punished by being cut off from the people of God, because he did not preserve the purity of the relationship between brothers and sisters.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: The fountain of her blood: her reproductive organs from which the blood flows.

If a man has a physical relationship with his wife during her monthly period, or during her illness with a disease that causes her to bleed, and does so deliberately and not by oversight (ch. 15:24, 18:19), both of them are punished by being cut off from the people of God, because they indulged in lust even though the woman's health condition did not suit such a union.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: He also warns against marrying a maternal or paternal aunt, because she is among the relatives whom it is forbidden to marry (ch. 18:12, 13, ch. 18:6). If two dare to enter into this wrong relationship, they bear the guilt of this sin and its punishment, which is being cut off from the people of God.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: If a man marries his uncle's wife, he has transgressed the law of forbidden marriages, for she stands in the place of his aunt, that is, his mother. They bear the punishment of this sin, which is most likely being cut off from the people of God, in addition to their becoming childless, and this means:
1- God strikes them with barrenness, so that they have no children.
2- Or their children born of them die.
3- Or the children born are considered illegitimate, because God is not pleased with this relationship.

entries.section: (2) The punishment for dishonoring parents and for adultery

paragraphs.text: The Law had already declared the prohibition of marrying the wife of a brother, whether during his lifetime if he had divorced her, or after his death if she had borne children (ch. 18:16). If this happens, it is considered a crime and an uncleanness, because he has dishonored his brother, that is, he did not respect the feelings of brotherhood, and their punishment is childlessness, as was explained in the previous verse.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: God reminds them of the importance of keeping His commandments and worshiping Him so that they may remain in the Promised Land, and of not taking part in the worship of idols like the pagan inhabitants of the land, lest this holy land vomit them out, that is, the land which God sanctified by dwelling in it and by their holy worship. Because God hated the evils of the original inhabitants of the land, He drove them out of it and settled the children of Israel in it in their place, because they were distinguished by the worship of God and by holiness, so they received the good things of the land, which is described as flowing with milk and honey.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: God reaffirms to them the law of the foods permitted from clean animals and birds, together with keeping away from eating the unclean animals and birds which He distinguished, that is, defined, for them.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: God demands holiness of them, that is, that they worship Him alone and keep away from all evil, for two reasons:
1- Because He is holy and righteous, and they can live with Him and enjoy fellowship with Him.
2- Because God has distinguished them from the other peoples with many blessings, and therefore they have no need of the pagan gods, who are demons, and of all their evils that corrupt the soul.

Remember, when Satan presents any sin to you, that the holy God, your heavenly Father, is looking at you. Do not defile yourself with sin and separate yourself from Him, so that you are deprived of His blessings, His fellowship and His love. Hold fast to holiness, for it is your means of enjoying peace and joy forever.

entries.section: (3) By holiness they dwell in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: The gravity of the sin of dealing with demons, who are called familiar spirits, and of those who deal with them, who are called sorcerers, was spoken of before (ch. 19:31).
