If anyone transgresses this commandment and deals with demons, his guilt is great and he is punished by death by stoning.
The Book of Exodus: The holiness of the priests

The Law forbids the priest to take part in the burial rites of any person, because death is connected with sin and is therefore considered an uncleanness, and whoever touches or takes part in the burial of a dead person becomes unclean. The priest is the example of holiness for all the people.
The priest is allowed an exception for seven near relatives, whom he may take part in burying without being defiled, because he is directly responsible for them. These relatives are:
The father, the mother, the son, the daughter, the brother, the unmarried sister, and the wife.

As for the married sister, her husband is responsible for her. As for the wife, as is made clear in (v. 4), he is not defiled by taking part in her burial, because he and she are one flesh, and she is the one referred to as his kin (v. 4). But as for the rest of the kin and relatives, whatever their rank, he must not defile himself by burying them.
He warns them against practices that were offered to the pagan gods, such as:
1- Making a bald spot on the head by shaving all sides of the head and leaving a circle of hair on top of the head.
2- Shaving the hair from the sides of the beard, that is, the two sides, and leaving the middle part on the chin, in order to please the gods.
3- Making cuttings in the various parts of the body.
If the whole people are forbidden to do these pagan practices, how much more the priest, who is their highest example, so that his worship is wholly for God and not for idols.
Here He declares the importance of the holiness of the priests and of their keeping away from burying the dead or from pagan practices, for the following reasons:
1- Because their lives are set apart, consecrated and holy to God.
2- Because they are the highest example for the people in hallowing the name of the Lord, so that the people may follow their example.
3- Because they offer the offerings and burnt offerings to God in His house, and because of their greatness, the one who offers them needs to be holy.

Do not forget that you are holy to God, so give Him your whole heart and not sin and the world. And if you sin, wash your heart by repentance and confession, and sanctify also your thoughts, your words and your deeds, so that you may be an example for others and a light to the world.
The priest represents perfection and is an example for the people, so he must also be careful about his marriage:
1- The wife he chooses must not be known among the people for immorality, lest she return to her immorality and cause the people and her husband to stumble.
2- She must not be defiled by any evil deed well known among the people, such as theft, lest she trouble the priest by her conduct and cause the people to stumble.
3- His wife must not have been married before and divorced, lest the reason for her divorce was bad conduct and she return to it.

God addresses the people and asks them to regard the priest as holy in their eyes, because he offers the offerings of the Lord, and God sanctified him on the day of his ordination. The effect of the people's hallowing of the priest appears in: The Book of Exodus
1- Respecting him.
2- Following his example.

Here He stresses the importance of the priest's taking care in raising his children, because he is an example for the people, and therefore He makes the punishment severe for the priest's daughter if she falls into immorality. If any virgin commits adultery, she is stoned, but the priest's daughter is burned with fire, as a declaration of God's anger against her, to wipe out the stumbling block she could cause the people, and as a declaration of the priest's rejection of this shameful conduct, because her immorality has defiled the house of the priest and become a disgrace and an object of the people's mockery. Her burning with fire confirms the purity of the priest and puts the fear of God in the hearts of the people.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: The chief priest: the high priest.

In this verse and the following verses God speaks about the high priest, on whose head the oil was poured on the day of his consecration, whose hand was filled, that is, who began to offer the sacrifices, and who put on the splendid garments of the high priest. He is the highest example for the priests and the people, and he is responsible for the care of the priests. So he must not indulge in displays of grief and distress by uncovering his head and tearing his clothes, as some of the people do, because his sorrows have hope, and by his composure he is an example to others.
The high priest is a type of Christ, so he does not uncover his head, that is, his dignity, and does not tear his clothes, which signify the Church.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: God forbids him to take part in the burial rites of any dead person, even if it is his father or mother. He is an example of purity and of keeping away from any uncleanness, although the ordinary priest is permitted to take part in the burial of the seven near relatives (vv. 2-4).

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: The sanctuary: the tabernacle of meeting.

Here He confirms that the high priest is not to take part in anyone's funeral or in any trouble that requires him to go out from the tabernacle of meeting, because he serves God in His house, and it is not right for him to go out and leave the service, for it is more important than any other worldly work. He supports this by the fact that upon his head are the crowns of glory and honor which he received through the pouring of the oil on his head, so that he may come forward and stand in the presence of God; therefore it is not right for him to leave God for any reason.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: It is required in the choice of his wife that she be a virgin, for he is a type of Christ, who betrothed the Church to Himself as a virgin, so that all her feelings and her love are for Him.

He does not marry a widow, lest she make a comparison between him and her first husband, which may cause problems. And he does not marry a divorced woman, that is, one who entered into problems with her first husband, so that she may be at peace and suitable for union with this great position of leadership, the position of the high priest.
And he does not marry a woman of immorality who has been defiled by this sin, for she does not suit this great position, which needs great purity.
This virgin must of course be a Jewess, that is, from his own people, because foreign women were associated with the worship of idols; that is, she ought to be a believer in God and live with Him.

entries.section: (2) The holiness of the high priest

paragraphs.text: One of the reasons for the care in choosing the wife is that the high priest may have blessed offspring, not defiled because of the morals and conduct of their mother, so that he does not expose his position of leadership to the talk of the people, or to being a stumbling block for him. In addition, his sons will be priests, and if an impure and careless mother raises them, they will be wicked. God affirms that He has sanctified him and set him apart for His service, so his whole family must be pure and set apart for Him.
The Book of Exodus

Care for the holiness of your home, your wife and your children, by looking after them, showing them love, and binding them to the Church, so that it may be a Christian home that glorifies God, and you may be an example to those around you and enjoy an atmosphere that helps you grow spiritually.

Here He mentions the physical conditions that must be met by the priest so that he may be without blemish, for he is a type of Christ, the Lamb without blemish, and so that his permanent defect may not hinder him from the service of God. This applies throughout the service of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levites "in their generations", that is, it is not applied in the New Testament, because these physical defects signify spiritual defects; if the latter, the spiritual ones, are found in the New Testament, he is barred from the priesthood.

Here He specifies the physical defects that bar from the priesthood. They are not applied in the New Testament, but if a disability exists that prevents the priest from carrying out his service, in that case he is barred only from the priesthood. The grounds for exclusion in the Old Testament are:
1- A blind man: this signifies the lack of spiritual insight and spiritual understanding.
2- A lame man: this signifies the uprightness lacking in his conduct.
3- One who has a flat nose: that is, one with a deformity of the nose, so that he cannot distinguish well by smell; this signifies weakness in distinguishing between right and wrong.
4- One who has anything superfluous: that is, one who has any excess growth on his body, such as an extra finger; this signifies excessive preoccupation with the world.

5- One who has a broken foot or broken hand: this would hinder him from performing his service, and it appears that the setting of fractures at that time was not completely possible; it signifies weakness in the capacity for spiritual work and sound conduct.
6- Crookbackt: that is, one with a bowed back, and this prevents him from performing the service successfully. It signifies one burdened with the load of many sins on his back who does not feel them.

7- A dwarf: that is, one from whom some part of his body is missing, such as the nose or a finger. The dwarf is counted as one of its kinds, and this hinders him from his service and signifies the person who is lacking in his spiritual relationship with God.
8- One who has a blemish in his eye: this is a white cloud that obscures sight and signifies weakness in spiritual discernment.
9- Scurvy: this is one who has a skin disease that makes him inclined to scratch. It signifies one on whom the marks of sin appear and who causes others to stumble.
10- Scabbed: this is one who has patches differing from the color of the skin on his face and on some parts of his body. It signifies one whose life sin disfigures and who causes others to stumble.

11- Having his stones broken: this is one to whom an accident has happened, or who was struck on his testicles, or who has a disease that weakens them. It signifies spiritual weakness and preoccupation with lusts.

In conclusion, God affirms that the priest should have no physical defects, so that they do not hinder him from his service and so that the people may feel that he is perfect, because their outlook in the Old Testament was material. In addition, some of them thought that physical defects were due to sin; this is a mistaken belief, but it existed among them and could confuse their minds concerning the priest and cause him trouble.
The Book of Exodus
The most holy and the holy: the foods that the priest takes from the house of the Lord, which are most holy or holy and set apart for him.

If a priest of the seed of Aaron has a physical defect among the defects mentioned above and is not permitted to serve in the house of the Lord, he is nevertheless not deprived of his portion of the food and drink that the priest receives, because he does no material work that brings him profit, just as the New Testament teaches that the expenses of the priest's life be provided (1 Cor 9:
11-14), even if he is struck by illness or reaches old age, which hinders him from service.

Here He confirms that one who has a defect is not permitted to enter the sanctuary to serve God and to see the veil that separates the sanctuary from the Holy of Holies. Nor may he approach the bronze altar to offer sacrifices, because if he dared and performed a service, he would defile the place by breaking the commandments of God, who sanctified the place and the servants who work in it and barred the one who has a defect from service.

Moses taught Aaron and his sons all the preceding commandments concerning the sanctification of the priests mentioned in this chapter, and likewise taught the people all the commandments of God mentioned in the preceding chapters. He is a faithful servant who carries out his work with care.

Examine yourself to discover your spiritual defects and your weaknesses of soul, then ask for God's help and the guidance of your father of confession to correct them. And know that God is able to forgive your sins, however many they are, and to complete what is lacking in you, whatever you suffer from.
Conditions for the sacrifices offered to God

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Separate themselves: respect and revere.

The holy things of the children of Israel: the foods that the priests eat from the offerings and sacrifices of the children of Israel to God. God asked Moses to teach Aaron and his sons the priests to respect the holy things of God, eating them with fear and reverence and not like the rest of their foods, for in this eating of theirs they perform a divine work, since they proclaim God's acceptance The Book of Exodus of the sacrifices and offerings of the people, and they feel that God is the Giver of this food and its Blesser, so they eat it with joy and humility. For their eating these holy things with greed or with evil desire, as if it were ordinary food, is a defiling and a despising of God.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: To confirm the reverence due from the priests and their households for the Lord's portion of the foods which they eat, He warns them against eating of it if any of them has an uncleanness for any of the reasons mentioned previously in this book. Whoever makes light of it and eats of these foods while his uncleanness is upon him is cut off from the priesthood and deprived of service before God, that is, he is removed far from God, because he has defiled His holy things.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: He gives examples of cases of uncleanness that are barred from eating the holy things of God, which are:
1- The priest who is afflicted with leprosy (ch. 13, 14).
2- The priest who is afflicted with a discharge (ch. 15:1-15).
3- The priest who touches a dead person or something belonging to him (ch. 21).
4- A priest who has had marital relations with his wife (ch. 15:16-18).
5- A priest who has touched an unclean creeping animal, or anything touched by the carcass of that unclean animal (ch. 11:24-44).
6- A priest who has touched an unclean person, with any kind of uncleanness.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: If any priest is made unclean by any of the preceding uncleannesses or by any other kind of uncleanness, he remains unclean until evening, then he washes his whole body, and after that he is permitted to eat of the holy things of God, which are his food.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: All the people were forbidden to eat animals that had died or been torn by beasts, because their blood is in them (ch. 17:15, 16); how much more is the priest not permitted to eat of them, lest he defile himself.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: My ordinance: My worship and My statutes.
God warns His priests to be exacting in applying His Law in their worship of Him; as for whoever makes light of it, he exposes himself to death as the punishment for despising the Law of God.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: The portion of the priests from the sacrifices and offerings of God is eaten by him and his seed, that is, his wife and his children only, and it is not permitted for any of the following to eat of it:
1- Strangers, that is, Jews who are not of the seed of the priests (Num 1:15).
2- Sojourners, that is, guests, whether they are Jews or non-Jews.
3- Hired servants, that is, those who work for the priests, whether temporary slaves or day laborers, Jews or non-Jews.

In sum, these holy foods (such as his portion of the peace offering) are enjoyed only by the priest and his household, as a divine grace with which God favors the priest and his household, and they signify the blessing of God given to the priests and servants.

If you serve God and labor for His sake, know that He is rich and is not indebted to anyone, but He will bless you with many blessings by which you are distinguished from others, not only material blessings but rather spiritual blessings that advance you on the road to the Kingdom; so seize every opportunity to offer Him your love.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Those permitted to eat of the holy things of God, other than the priest's household, are:
1- The slaves whom the priest bought and circumcised, so that they became Jews residing permanently with the priest.
2- Slaves born to male and female slaves who reside permanently in the priest's house; these are circumcised and permitted to eat.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: The priest's daughter eats of the holy things of God, and if she marries a priest she will also eat of them, but if she marries a stranger, that is, a Jew who is not of the priests, she is under his care and belongs to him, and so she is deprived of the food of her father's house, which is the holy things of God.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: It is also permitted to eat of the holy things for the following:
1- The priest's daughter who married a stranger and then he divorced her, so she returned to her father's house.

2- The widow whose stranger husband died and who bore no children by him, so she returned to her father's house. The Book of Exodus But the widow who bore children, whether she returned to her father's house or did not return, does not eat of the holy things, neither she nor her children, because her husband's family are responsible to provide for her.
3- If the widow's children die, she returns to her father's house and is permitted to eat of the holy things.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: If any Jewish person who is not of the seed of the priests eats of the holy things of God by oversight, that is, unintentionally, he has sinned, and he is to do the following:
1- He offers a trespass offering, a ram for God.
2- He gives food like what he ate and adds a fifth to it, as compensation and an apology for his error.

entries.section: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: If some of the people sin and eat by oversight of the holy things of God that are set apart for the priests, or if the priests sin and eat of these holy things while they are unclean, then they:
1- Profane the name of God and do not respect it.
2- Defile the whole people, because they are individuals of it.
This makes a person careful in his worship and conduct, because his sin offends God and his whole family and community, and even encourages others to it, so that he spreads sin among people.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Their freewill offerings: the voluntary offerings other than those the Law prescribes, which are considered an offering of love to God in thanks for His kindnesses.

The conditions of the sacrifice that the Law prescribed were explained in the first chapters of this book, and the children of Israel used to offer additional offerings, such as vows, which are tied to a particular request from God, or freewill offerings, which are offerings of love to Him. God also requires that these be:
1- From the herd, the sheep or the goats, which are the clean animals that the Law prescribed.
2- A male, which signifies strength, so that the best is offered to God.
3- Perfect: that is, without blemish, as a type of Christ, who is without sin and offered Himself as a sacrifice for us on the Cross.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: The vow or freewill sacrifice was offered as a peace offering with these preceding conditions, out of love for God and to obtain His pleasure and blessing; but if anyone makes light of these conditions, this is considered making light of God and brings His anger upon him.
Having pustules: one who has pustules, that is, boils.
Spotted: one who has black dots, that is, freckles.
God forbids the offering of a sacrifice that has any blemish, and He specifies these blemishes, which are:
1- Blind.
2- Broken: having any part of its legs or bones broken.
3- One that has a wound, new or old, which left a clear mark.
4- Having pustules, because pustules mar its appearance.
5- Scabbed: one that has been afflicted with scab disease.
6- Spotted: that is, one whose skin has many patches that mar its appearance.
So no sacrifice with these blemishes is to be brought near on the altar of God.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Having anything superfluous: excessive length in one of the bones, or extra fingers.
The Book of Exodus Lacking in his parts: excessive smallness of the body.

It is not permitted to offer one with anything superfluous or one that is lacking in its parts in these sacrifices which the Law prescribes or in vows, but it is permitted in the case of the freewill offering, because it is a gift of love offered to God.

The peace offering and vows must be without blemish, because they signify Christ, but the freewill offering is a gift from man to God and may have small weaknesses, such as having anything superfluous or being lacking in its parts, because it signifies the weakness of man.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Bruised testicles: one whose testicle was struck so that it was damaged.
Crushed: its testicle was ruined by crushing.
Cut: its testicle was removed and cut off.
The Law forbids the offering of an animal whose testicle is damaged as a sacrifice to God, because it signifies the inability to beget, that is, the lack of spiritual fruit.
And God forbids them to castrate animals in any way, since some pagan worship commanded this.

entries.section: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

paragraphs.text: From a stranger's hand: the animals bought from non-Jews.

God forbids them to buy animals that have blemishes, as was mentioned in the preceding verses, in order to offer them as sacrifices to God, so that they may obtain His pleasure with good and perfect sacrifices; for offering blemished sacrifices is making light of God and of His commands.

Give God the best of what you have, whether in time or in material gifts, so that your perfect love for Him may appear; then the house of God will be better than your own house, and you will care for the brethren of the Lord more than you care for yourself, or at least as you care for yourself.

In His commandments to Moses about offering sacrifices, God added that an animal is not to be offered before seven days from its birth, so that it will have enjoyed suckling from its mother during these days, which is important nourishment for the newborn, and so that its mother also may enjoy it and her motherhood be satisfied. To this extent the mercy of God appears in His Law, so that He may teach us kindness to animals, and all the more that we have compassion on our brothers and sisters, human beings. For this reason the Jews did not slaughter an animal to eat it before seven days from its birth.

May you feel the feelings of others around you, and find excuses for them in their errors and shortcomings, and be longsuffering toward them, and provide for their needs before they ask for them. And compassion is to be shown to all, even animals, because a merciful heart is merciful to the great and the small, the rich and the poor, man and animal.

To complete the feelings of mercy, the Law commands that the mother animal not be slaughtered with her young in one day; it is enough that the animal has lost its young or lost its mother, so it is not to be offered for slaughter on the same day, because it is affected by this loss. This is the divine mercy that God expects us to practice with one another, so that we are not harsh to a person and his child at the same time.
The Book of Exodus

If a person offers a thank offering to God, that is, a peace offering, his purpose is to please God and obtain His blessing in his life; therefore he adheres to all the conditions previously mentioned in this book, which mean offering the best that he has, and that it be without blemish.

Here He stresses the importance of eating the peace offering on the same day, as came in (ch. 7:15), for it signifies the sacrifice of the Eucharist in the New Testament, which is eaten on the same day.

At the end of this chapter God asks them to be committed to carrying out His commandments in all their sacrifices, thereby declaring their fear of God and their love for Him, because any violation of His laws is contempt for and defiling of His name before themselves and before the peoples around them. And He reminds them of His love and care for them, for it is He who brought them out of Egypt with great power and preserved them in the wilderness, so they must live for Him and obey His commandments.
The feasts. First: the idea of the feast:
The word feast means a witness or an assembly, and the feasts are called the appointed seasons or religious celebrations, and what is meant by them is:
1- Stopping work and devoting oneself to the worship of God.
2- Remembering important spiritual events that bind people to the worship of God, to loving Him and to thanking Him for His kindnesses.

3- The celebrations in the Old Testament signify Christ the Savior, His redemption and His blessing in our lives, in addition to many spiritual meanings which we will speak about in detail with each feast.
Second: in the New Testament:

Because feasts are a spiritual idea necessary for the spiritual person, they continued in the New Testament also, but their occasions changed, since they came to center on the One signified, who is Christ, in addition to the feasts of the saints who lived their lives in faith in Christ.
Third: the feasts that the Law prescribed:
A- Weekly feasts: this is the Sabbath day (Ex 20:8-11), which the Jews keep as a feast and on which they worship God in their homes.
B- Monthly feasts: these are the beginnings of the months, called the new moons (Num 10:10, 28:11-15), on which they worship God and offer Him offerings, whether for the Temple or for the poor.
C- Yearly feasts, which include:
1- The Feast of the Passover on the fourteenth of the first month (Ex 12).
2- The Feast of Unleavened Bread, which follows the Feast of the Passover, for seven days (Ex 13).
3- The Feast of the Firstfruits on the eighteenth day of the second month, a remembrance of the offering of the first ripe ear of grain.
4- The Feast of Pentecost, called the Feast of Weeks, which falls in the sixth month (Ex 23:16).
5- The Feast of Trumpets, which falls at the beginning of the seventh month (Lev 23:23, 24).
6- The Day of Atonement, which falls on the tenth day of the seventh month (Lev 16).

7- The Feast of Tabernacles, which falls on the fifteenth day of the seventh month (Lev 23:33-36). These months are the months of the religious year, whereas the first of the months of the civil year is the one corresponding to the seventh month of the religious year.
God commanded the carrying out of these feasts in two stages:
The first stage: this is immediately after the giving of the Law in the wilderness of Sinai, and it comprises the feasts of the Sabbath, the Passover, Unleavened Bread, Trumpets and the Atonement.

The second stage: this is after their entry into the land of Canaan, and it comprises the feasts of the Firstfruits, Pentecost and Tabernacles. And God commanded that all the males of the children of Israel appear at His house at three feasts (Ex 23:14-17), which are:
1- The Feast of the Passover.
2- The Feast of Pentecost.
3- The Feast of Tabernacles.
The males represented the whole family, and the woman also was permitted to attend these feasts, and if she did not attend, the male acted on her behalf.
D- Periodic feasts: that is, every several years, and they are:
1- The seventh year (Ex 23:10, 11, Lev 25:1-7).

2- The year of Jubilee, that is, the fiftieth year (Lev 25:8-22). It is to be noted that God commanded these feasts to Moses and he wrote them in the books of Exodus, Leviticus and Numbers. Fourth: feasts added by the Jews: these are according to their historical occurrence, for important events passed in the life of the Jews and they added other feasts, which are:
1- The Feast of the Dedication of Solomon's Temple after he built it, in the seventh month (1 Kgs 8:2).
2- The remembrance of the restoration of the Temple at the hand of Zerubbabel in the twelfth month (Ezra 6:15).
3- The Feast of the Renewal of the Temple, which Judas Maccabeus ordained, on the twenty-fifth of the ninth month, lasting eight days (1 Macc 4:59), (Jn 10:22).
4- The remembrance of the dedication of the Temple of Herod the Great (Jn 2:20).

5- The two feasts of Purim, on the fourteenth and fifteenth of the twelfth month, which Esther and Mordecai ordained in remembrance of God's deliverance of the children of Israel from the plot of Haman (Esth 9:29-32).

6- The day which the Jews ordained in remembrance of Judith's victory over Holofernes, the commander of the armies of the Assyrians, and the deliverance of the children of Israel from him (Jdt 16:31).
7- The feast of the appearance of the holy fire in the days of Nehemiah (2 Macc 1:18).
8- The remembrance of their victory over Nicanor the commander at the hand of Judas Maccabeus on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month (1 Macc 7:48, 49).

This is an introduction that God gives about the feasts. He calls them seasons and also holy convocations, which are proclaimed to all the people by means of trumpets so that they may take notice and be occupied with the feast rather than their ordinary work, to remember the spiritual meaning that God intends by the feast.
Sabbath: rest.

Just as God rested from His works in the creation of the world on the seventh day, so He commanded in the Fourth Commandment to keep the Sabbath day holy, that is, to set it apart for the worship of God. Material work is not done on it, but prayers are lifted up and sacrifices are offered, and only the necessary material tasks are done, such as giving food and drink to their animals.

The Jews laid down many specific material rules for the Sabbath, to prevent work and to permit walking a set distance ... and they neglected the spiritual side. But Christ made clear that the purpose of the Sabbath is the worship and service of God and not merely stopping work (Mt 12:9-13). In the New Testament the glory of Sunday surpassed that of the Sabbath, because on it Christ rose from the dead; therefore the Lord's Day in the New Testament is Sunday, while the Sabbath day is also honored because on it God completed the creation of the world and rested, that is, was pleased with what He had made, so we please Him by worship and service.

Take care to distinguish the Lord's Day with more worship and service than the other days, remembering His love for you, for He rose to raise you from the preoccupations of the world and to let you enjoy fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (2) The Feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: After mentioning the Sabbath day, which the Ten Commandments enjoin, He proclaimed the great feasts of the Jews, which are seven:
1- The Feast of the Passover (v. 5)
2- The Feast of Unleavened Bread (vv. 6-8)
3- The Feast of Firstfruits (vv. 9-14)
4- The Feast of Pentecost (vv. 15-22)
5- The Feast of Trumpets (vv. 23-25)
6- The Feast of Atonement (vv. 26-32)
7- The Feast of Tabernacles (vv. 33-36)

entries.section: (2) The Feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: The Feast of the Passover is a remembrance of what they did when they went out of the land of Egypt, where God rescued them from slavery and saved their firstborn from death. It was held on the fourteenth day of the first month, which is the month of Abib, called Nisan after the captivity. It is the first month of the religious year, which corresponds to the seventh month of the civil year, and corresponds today to the months of March and April. This feast was already mentioned and explained in (Ex 12:1-14), and is also mentioned in (Num 28) and (Deut 16:6). It was held between the two evenings, that is, between the ninth and the eleventh hour by Jewish reckoning, which is between three and five in the afternoon by present-day reckoning. It clearly signifies Christ the Redeemer (1 Cor 5:7), who died for us on the Cross.

entries.section: (2) The Feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: The Feast of Unleavened Bread is the second feast of the Jews and follows the Passover directly, that is, on the fifteenth day of the first month, and is kept for seven days, in remembrance of the children of Israel taking their dough before it was leavened and going out quickly from Egypt. Its taste is not as good as leavened bread, so it signifies the misery that the children of Israel suffered in Egypt. Unleavened bread also signifies purity and sincerity, and Christ, who was distinguished by these qualities (1 Cor 5:8). In the Church of the New Testament, however, leavened bread is offered, because Christ offered leavened bread on Maundy Thursday. Leaven signifies evil, for Christ bore our sins on the Cross and died for us.

entries.section: (2) The Feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread

paragraphs.text: The Feast of Unleavened Bread is kept on the first day, that is, the fifteenth, and the seventh, that is, the twenty-first of the first month, and on them they free themselves for worship and leave their material work. During the days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread these sacrifices are offered every day (Num 28:17-25:)

1- Burnt offerings, which are two young bullocks, one ram and seven lambs of the first year, in addition to three tenths of flour mingled with oil for each bullock, two tenths for the ram, and one tenth for each lamb.
2- A sin offering, which is a kid of the goats.
3- The daily burnt offering with its drink offerings in the morning and evening (Num 28:3-10).
4- Freewill offerings (Deut 16:16, 17).

Remember every morning Christ, who died for you so that you might live for Him, when you pray the prime hour and remember His holy Resurrection, so that your aim on this day is to respond to His love with worship and doing good.

The third feast is the Feast of Firstfruits, that is, offering the first sheaf of the harvest of their crops, which was of barley because it ripens before other crops such as wheat. Of course this feast began after the children of Israel entered the Promised Land and cultivated the land.
Offering the firstfruits of animals and crops has spiritual meanings, the most important of which are:
1- Declaring that God is the giver of all good things, of animals and of plants, so we give Him from His own hand.
2- Thanking God for His gifts.
3- God's blessing on the remainder that man uses.
4- Supporting the priests and the Levites consecrated to the service of the temple.
And this feast falls within the Feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread.
Wave: he carries it on his hands and moves it in the four directions, that is, it is offered to God who fills every place.
The priest takes the sheaf and waves it before God in one of the following ways:
1- He waves the sheaf as it is, with its ears, after dipping it in oil, then takes a handful of it and offers it on the altar with the frankincense, and the rest is eaten by him and the priests.

2- The sheaf is beaten with a rod to separate the grains from the straw, then the grains are roasted on the fire and oil is put on them, and then the priest offers a handful of it on the altar with the frankincense, and the rest is eaten by the priests.
3- The grains are ground and the flour is kneaded with oil, then the priest takes a handful of it and offers it with the frankincense on the altar, and the rest is eaten by the priests.
And the sheaf of firstfruits signifies Christ, the Firstborn among many brethren, who offered Himself on the Cross to the Father and redeemed us.
The sheaf is offered on the morrow after the Sabbath, and what is meant by the morrow after the Sabbath is:
1- Either the Sunday following the Sabbath that falls during the days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, as the Sadducees among the Jews hold.

2- Counting the first day of Unleavened Bread, which is the fifteenth of the first month, as the day of rest on which no work is done and which is consecrated to God, so that it is the Sabbath, because the word sabbath means rest; consequently the Feast of Firstfruits is the sixteenth day of the first month, and this is the opinion of the Pharisees.
At the Feast of Firstfruits, in addition to the first sheaf of the harvest, the following are offered:
1- A he lamb without blemish of the first year as a burnt offering.
2- Two tenths of fine flour mingled with oil, which equals 6.4 liters, and wine is poured on it in the amount of a fourth part of a hin, that is, one liter.

The lamb signifies Christ the Redeemer, who pleased the Father by the sacrifice of Himself; the flour mingled with oil signifies the purity of the life of Christ in the flesh, in which is the oil, that is, the Holy Spirit; and the wine signifies the joy that Christ brought into our hearts by His redemption.
To the offerings of the Feast of Firstfruits are added the offerings that are offered in the days of Unleavened Bread, mentioned in the explanation of (vv. 7, 8).
Parched corn: green grains of wheat after being roasted or grilled.
Green ears: green ears of wheat.

The Law forbids eating of the grains of the new harvest, barley or wheat, in any form before the first sheaf is offered at the Feast of Firstfruits, and during the days of Unleavened Bread they eat from the old harvest, because it is God who takes first from the harvest, and so blesses the rest, and then the people eat of it.

The Feast of Firstfruits signifies the Resurrection of Christ, who rose as the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, and it comes on the third day of the Passover. And while the Jews were celebrating the Feast of Firstfruits in the year of the crucifixion of Christ, He rose from the dead on the same day, so the Feast of Firstfruits signifies His Resurrection.

Make sure that God has a share in all your good things, so you give Him the firstfruits of your money, your possessions, your crops and all that He gives you, and so receive His blessing in your life; and offer firstfruits of every kind to the needy, so that all rejoice with one heart because they are members of the one body of Christ, that is, the Church.
The morrow after the Sabbath: Sunday.

The day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering: that is, the day of the Feast of Firstfruits, which is the first of the days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread and which follows the Passover, as we mentioned.
Seven sabbaths: 49 days.
The morrow after the seventh sabbath: corresponds to the fiftieth day from the Feast of Firstfruits.

The day of Pentecost comes fifty days after the Feast of Firstfruits and is a Sunday, just as the Feast of Firstfruits is a Sunday, and at the Feast of Pentecost special offerings are brought near to God.

The Feast of the Fiftieth Day is also called the Feast of Pentecost, whose meaning in the Greek language is fiftieth (Acts 2:1, 20:16); it is also called the Feast of Weeks because it comes seven weeks after the Feast of Firstfruits (Ex 34:22, Deut 16:10). It is also called the Feast of Harvest because on it the harvest of wheat and the rest of the winter crops is completed (Ex 23:16). They also call it the Feast of Firstfruits because on it the firstfruits of the wheat harvest are offered.

It is clear that the celebration of this feast began after the children of Israel entered the Promised Land and cultivated wheat and the other crops. The Feast of Pentecost is one of the most important feasts among the Jews, because on it all the men must come to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, as also happens at the Feasts of the Passover and Tabernacles.

This feast comes in the third month of the religious year, which is called Sivan; it corresponds to the ninth month of the civil year and today corresponds to the months of May and June. The purpose of this feast is:
1- To thank God for His gifts of the winter crops, the most important of which is wheat, and that He completed His work with His people and gave them His good things.
2- A remembrance of God's giving the commandments to Moses on the mountain, since the Jews believed that the commandments were given fifty days after their departure from the land of Egypt.

Because of the importance of this feast, the Jews offered repentance and confession of their sins and washed on it as a symbol of their purity, in addition to spending the night of the feast in praising God.

At the end of (v. 16) it says "ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the LORD," and what is meant is offering the first sheaf of the wheat harvest, which is apart from the first offering, that is, the first sheaf of the barley harvest, which they offered at the Feast of Firstfruits.

The Feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread signify the toil and hardship that the children of Israel endured in slavery in Egypt, from which God brought them out by the plague on the firstborn, in which they slaughtered the Passover. The Feasts of Firstfruits and Pentecost signify joy at receiving God's blessings and good things. And if the Feast of the Passover signifies the death of Christ on the Cross and the Feast of Firstfruits signifies His Resurrection, then the Feast of Pentecost signifies the descent of the Holy Spirit, who in fact descended on the Church on it and founded it.
Your habitations: your fields in the land of Canaan.
Bread: leavened flour.
Two tenth deals: each loaf is made of a tenth of an ephah, that is, 2.3 liters.

They used to make two large loaves, each about 70 cm by 40 cm in size and about 10 cm thick, baked with leavened flour because they represent their daily food, and they offer them to God to bless all their foods. No part of them is offered on the altar, because no leaven is placed on the altar, as it signifies evil (Lev 2:11); so they are only waved before God, that is, the priests carry them on their hands and move them in the four directions of the world, declaring God's blessing on all their fields and foods, and then the priests eat them as a symbol of God's acceptance of their offerings. The two loaves signify:
1- God's blessing on their earthly life, that is, their material work, and also their heavenly life, that is, their worship of God.
2- The two loaves signify the Jews and the Gentiles, for Christ came for the salvation of the whole world.
3- The number (2) signifies love, that is, their love for God and for one another.
4- The priests' eating of the two loaves signifies God's blessing in the sacrament of the priesthood, to give the priests strength to carry out their service.
The offerings that are offered at this feast are:
a- Basic offerings, which are those mentioned here in the Book of Leviticus, and include:
1- A burnt offering consisting of:
A young bullock with its offering, which is three tenths of flour mingled with oil, as mentioned in (Num 28:26-31).
Two rams with their offerings, which are two tenths of flour mingled with oil for each ram.
Seven lambs of the first year, that is, each one a year old, with their offerings, which are a tenth of an ephah of flour mingled, that is, kneaded with oil, for each lamb.
2- A sin offering, which is a kid of the goats.
3- A peace offering, which is two lambs of the first year.
b- Additional sacrifices, which are those mentioned in the Book of Numbers (Num 28:26-31), and include:
1- A burnt offering, which is:
Two young bullocks with their offerings, which are three tenths of flour mingled with oil for each bullock.
A ram with its offering, which is two tenths of flour mingled with oil.
Seven lambs of the first year with their offerings, which are one tenth of flour mingled with oil for each lamb.
2- A sin offering, which is a kid of the goats.
c- Voluntary sacrifices, that is, freewill offerings, which the people offer to God for the priests and the Levites to eat of, and which are mentioned in the Book of Deuteronomy (Deut 16:9-12).
d- The daily burnt offering in the morning and evening, which is mentioned in (Ex 29:38-42).
The two lambs: what is meant is the two lambs of the peace offering.

The priest waves part of the sin offerings and peace offerings, which are the right thigh and the breast, that is, he moves them in the four directions before God, and then the priest and his household take them, with the two loaves also, as already mentioned in (v. 17). "They shall be holy to the LORD for the priest": the priest eats of them, as already explained in the sin offering (ch. 6:
24-30) and the peace offering (ch. 7:11-21).
The priests blow the trumpets and call the people to celebrate this feast, and each one leaves his material work and gives himself wholly to worship on this day.

Keeping this feast is a necessary command that God enjoined on the children of Israel to do throughout their days, as long as there are priests of the seed of Aaron, until Christ comes, whom all these sacrifices signify.

The full celebration of this feast was after they entered the land of Canaan and reaped the wheat, but the children of Israel began to celebrate it in part, by offering the sacrifices mentioned without the two loaves, in the wilderness of Sinai, in remembrance of Moses' receiving the Law.

In the New Testament we remember the feast in the Feast of Pentecost, which is the "Feast of the Fiftieth Day," the remembrance of the descent of the Holy Spirit on the Church, and we also remember Moses' receiving the Law in the prayer of the prostration, and much incense is offered in a large censer in remembrance of the sight of Mount Sinai full of fire and smoke when the Law was received.

Here God stresses His concern for the poor, so He repeats His commandment that He mentioned in (ch. 19:9, 10) and then repeated in (Deut 24:19-22), concerning the harvest of the fields: they leave the corners of their fields with their ears of grain, or the gleanings of the harvest, that is, the grains scattered on the ground, for the poor to gather, so that they may find food for themselves.

Let the feast be an opportunity to take care to visit the poor, the needy, the sick and everyone who is going through a distress, such as the death of a relative, so that you offer them love and they rejoice with you in this feast.

On the first day of the seventh month of the religious year, which corresponds to the first month in the civil year, which is the month of Tishri or Tishrin the First, also called Ethanim (1 Kgs 8:2), and which corresponds today to the month of September or October, the priests blow trumpets made of the horn of a sheep, with a mouthpiece of gold, or silver trumpets. At the Feast of Atonement, however, the trumpets were made of the horn of a ram. The trumpets have forms that are attached with the explanation.

The priests used to blow trumpets at this feast from its eve until the morning, and the people could blow other trumpets in their own places; on the Sabbath, however, the priests blew inside the house of the Lord and not outside it. The trumpets of the priests. This feast is called the Feast of Trumpets or the Feast of Shouting because they blow trumpets on it and shout with loud voices, glorifying God.

Blowing the trumpets at this feast, besides the other feasts, was used to gather the people at the beginnings of months and the various religious convocations, and also when calling them to war or for any other purposes. The Feast of Trumpets has many spiritual meanings, among them:
1- Thanking God for His kindnesses and mercies throughout the past year, for it is the close of the civil year and the gathering of the summer crops.

2- The feast coincides with the beginning of a new civil year and the sowing of the seeds of the winter crops, that is, the beginning of the new cultivation, so they ask God's blessing and prepare for a new spiritual beginning with Him, and remind Him of His covenants with their fathers so that He may bless them, and they pledge to live with Him.

3- The supreme council of the Jews (the Sanhedrin) decided that the Feast of Trumpets is a remembrance of the redemption of Isaac by a ram, that is, they remember God's redemption of them and His rescue of them from the slavery of Egypt, and all this signifies Christ the Redeemer in the fullness of time.
4- A remembrance of the giving of the Law on the mountain when they heard the sound of the trumpets (Ex 19:14-19); it declares the importance of the word of God and living by it.

5- This feast is a preparation for the following feasts in the same month, which are the Feast of Atonement and the Feast of Tabernacles, feasts of the greatest importance among the Jews, whose details will come shortly in this chapter.

6- This feast reminds them of keeping the seventh day, which is the Sabbath, holy, and of keeping the seventh year holy, and then the year of Jubilee, which comes after seven weeks, because this feast comes at the beginning of the seventh month.

7- In the Feast of Trumpets God calls His people to obtain salvation and confirms their hope in Him; it signifies their return from captivity and then faith in Christ (Isa 27:13), and it also signifies the Second Coming of Christ at the sound of the trumpets mentioned in the Book of Revelation (Rev 8-11).
Like the other feasts, the people free themselves for the worship of God and leave their material work.
The fire offering brought near to the Lord at the feast was:
a- The morning burnt offering and its offerings, as mentioned in (Ex 29:38-42, Num 28:1-8).
b- The offerings of the beginning of the month, which are mentioned in (Num 28:11-15) and include:
1- A burnt offering consisting of:
Two young bullocks with their offerings, three tenths of flour mingled with oil and half a hin of wine for each bullock.
A ram with its offering, two tenths of flour mingled with oil, with a third of a hin of wine poured on it.
Seven lambs of the first year with their offerings, one tenth of flour mingled with oil, and their drink offering is a fourth part of a hin of wine for each lamb.
2- A sin offering, which is a kid.

c- After the morning burnt offering and the offerings of the beginning of the month are offered, the trumpets are blown, and then the offerings of the Feast of Trumpets mentioned in (Num 29:1-6) are offered, which are:
Burnt offerings consisting of:
A bullock and its offering, which is three tenths of flour mingled with oil, with its drink offering, which is half a hin of wine.
A ram and its offering, two tenths of flour mingled with oil, and its drink offering, a third of a hin of wine.
Seven lambs of the first year and their offering, which is one tenth of flour mingled with oil, and their drink offering, a fourth part of a hin of wine.

Then the priest blesses the people with the words of blessing mentioned in (Num 6:24-26), and the people are bowing down, and then they depart to their homes. After the building of the Temple of Solomon, they used to go to the synagogues to hear readings from the Holy Scriptures and then return to their houses.
d- The people return in the evening to attend the offering of the evening burnt offering.

When God reminds you to return to Him and live with Him, do not neglect His voice, whether His speech is from the Holy Bible, or through one of the loved ones around you, or in any other form, for these are divine messages or trumpets that declare God's love and His longing for you.

This feast is also called the Feast of Forgiveness or of seeking forgiveness, and its date was the tenth of the seventh month of the religious year, which is the month of Tishrin the First, corresponding to the month of October today. It was a holy convocation on which the people refrained from their material work and gave themselves wholly to worship. They fasted on this day and humbled themselves with repentance and contrition before God. This feast signifies the redemption of Christ and His atonement for the sins of humanity, and corresponds to it in the New Testament Good Friday. At this feast they offer the offerings mentioned in detail in (ch. 16), which are:
a- The burnt offerings of the permanent morning and evening service.
b- The sacrifices of the feast, which are:
1- A bullock as a sin offering for the priests.
2- A goat as a sin offering for the people, in addition to the goat of Azazel, which is let go in the wilderness.
And also additional sacrifices, which are:
3- A burnt offering, which is a ram offered for the priests.
4- A bullock as a burnt offering for the people, with its offerings and drink offerings.
5- Seven lambs of the first year as a burnt offering for the people, with their offerings and drink offerings.
6- A sin offering, which is a goat.
All these sacrifices and their offerings were already explained in detail in (ch. 16).

Whoever refuses to humble himself, that is, to fast on this day, this means his lack of repentance and his need of God's forgiveness, so the Law commands that he be put to death for his refusal to believe in God and repent of his sins.

Likewise whoever makes light of this great feast and is occupied with his material work shows his lack of concern for repentance and God's forgiveness, so God declares that He will destroy him, that is, he dies by being put to death or dies in any form.

Therefore God commands abstaining from all material work at this feast, and this is to be applied throughout their lives and in the generations after them, until Christ comes and offers redemption and atonement for humanity on the Cross.
Ye shall celebrate your sabbath: you shall rest from your works.

God sets the time of freedom from work at this feast, which is the whole day, beginning from its eve, that is, the evening of the ninth day of the month, and then throughout the daytime of the tenth day.

Take care of your daily repentance before God so that you receive His forgiveness, renew your vigor and begin with new hope to make up for what you have missed, and set out on a positive spiritual life in His worship and service.

The Feast of Tabernacles is one of the important feasts among the Jews, and its date is the fifteenth of the seventh month of the religious year, which is the month of Tishrin the First, that is, Ethanim, corresponding to the month of October. It is kept for seven days in addition to the eighth day, which is a holy convocation; that is, the feast is kept eight days and the eighth day is an official holiday.

It is like the Feast of the Passover in its importance, since the Passover and Unleavened Bread are also kept eight days. Because of the importance of this feast it is mentioned several times in the Holy Bible: it is mentioned in the days of Solomon (2 Chr 8:13), in the days of Nehemiah (Neh 8:13-18) and in the days of Christ (Jn 7:2). This feast is also called the Feast of Ingathering, since on it all the summer crops and fruits such as grapes and olives are gathered; it is the third of the agricultural feasts after the Feasts of Firstfruits and Pentecost.
The spiritual meanings of this feast are:
1- Thanking God for His kindnesses after gathering all the crops of the year.

2- Remembering the days of their sojourn in the wilderness of Sinai when they lived in tents or movable booths; so that they would not forget God's kindnesses to them in bringing them to the Promised Land, they kept this feast.
3- This feast gives the meaning of the sojourn in the world and attachment to heavenly things, and this is a meaning that continues in the New Testament, as Zechariah prophesied (Zech 14:16) ....

This feast is the last of the feasts in the religious year and one of the three most important feasts, at which all the males of the people of God, on behalf of their families, must gather and stand before the house of God. These feasts are the Passover, Pentecost and then the Feast of Tabernacles.
They used to make these booths from the branches of trees (v. 42), and they have different forms as shown in the attached picture.
Different forms of booths

This feast is kept eight days. On the first and the eighth they free themselves for worship and do no material work, and on the six days between them their celebration of the feast and their dwelling in the booths continue. At this feast, on the first day, they gather the branches of trees and set up a shelter over the bronze altar, and bring water from the Pool of Siloam and pour it on the bronze altar over the morning burnt offering together with wine, so that they may remember not only their sojourn in the wilderness of Sinai but also their being given water to drink from the rock, which signifies Christ (1 Cor 10:4). The water signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who was poured out on the believers in the Church of the New Testament.
The fire offering of the Lord that is offered in the seven days is mentioned for us in the Book of Numbers in (Num 29:12-39), and it is: a- Burnt offerings:

1- Thirteen bullocks on the first day, decreasing by one bullock each day until the seventh day, when there are seven bullocks, and their total is seventy bullocks. And with each bullock, three tenths of flour mingled with oil.
2- Two rams each day, with two tenths of flour mingled with oil for each ram.
3- Fourteen lambs of the first year each day, with one tenth of flour mingled with oil for each lamb.
b- A sin offering: consisting of a kid of the goats.
c- The daily morning and evening burnt offering.
d- Peace offerings, vows and freewill offerings, which are the voluntary offerings from the people.

As for the eighth day of the Feast of Tabernacles, it is a solemn assembly, that is, giving oneself wholly to worship and leaving the daily work as happened on the first day, because if the Feast of Tabernacles signifies the sojourn in the world, then the sojourn must be joined with being occupied with the love of God and His worship, which is the purpose of life.
And the fire offerings of the Lord on this day, as the Book of Numbers mentions them for us (Num 29:35-39), are:
a- Burnt offerings:
1- A bullock with its offering, which is three tenths of flour mingled with oil.
2- One ram with its offering, two tenths of flour mingled with oil.
3- Seven lambs of the first year with their offerings, which are one tenth of flour mingled with oil for each lamb.
b- A sin offering, which is a kid of the goats.
c- The permanent burnt offering, morning and evening, with their offerings.
d- Peace offerings, vows and freewill offerings, which are the voluntary offerings that the people offer to God.

He closes with this verse, declaring that the above are the seven feasts of the Lord, which He calls seasons and holy convocations to God, with the sacrifices and offerings offered on each day of these feasts, as a showing of man's love and thanks to God.

In addition to the sacrifices offered at the feasts, the sacrifices offered on the days of the Sabbaths are also offered, on which the morning and evening burnt offering is double that of ordinary days. Likewise the voluntary offerings that the people offer to God are also added.

Here he stresses the importance of celebrating the Feast of Tabernacles, which they keep for eight days. The first day is a time of freedom for worship and a holiday from material work, after gathering the last harvest of the summer crops, and the eighth day is also a holiday.
The first day is the fifteenth of the seventh month and the eighth day is the twenty-second of it, so the feast extends eight days, but freedom for worship is only on the first and last day.
Thick: dense.
Willows: a plant that grows by watercourses.

He shows what happens at this feast, that is, the Feast of Tabernacles: the people gather palm branches and large tree branches and make booths from them, and complete them with small palm fronds and small tree branches, and decorate them with the cheerful fruit of trees, and they go to the Pool of Siloam to draw water and pour it on the bronze altar with wine, and they rejoice and go around the altar seven times, in remembrance of going around Jericho, so that they remember the Lord's victories with them and rejoice.
God stresses to them the celebration of this great feast for seven days throughout their days, as long as the Levitical priesthood stands.

All the Jews dwell in these booths that they make in the outer court of the house of God, in the streets of Jerusalem and on the mountains, and no one dwells in his house, so that they remember their sojourn from the world and their attachment to heaven.

He also reminds them of their dwelling in booths, the tents in which they lived forty years in the wilderness of Sinai, and of God's care for them with manna and quail and water from the rock and His protection of them from their enemies.
Moses told the people of God all that the Lord had commanded them concerning the feasts, so that they might carry it out and enjoy the worship of God and fellowship with Him.

Always remember, when you enjoy the material things of life, that God is the one who gives them to you, and thank Him; and on the other hand, discipline yourself in the use of material things so that your feelings of love toward God may be set free and nothing may hinder you from Him.

d- a sin offering, which is a goat.
